4.3
A1 policy transactions
4.3.1
Resources and payload objects
A1AP [i.3] describes how lifecycle management of an A1 policy is based on CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations
on a resource identified by a policy identifier (policyId) that is assigned by and is unique within the Non-RT RIC. The URI of
the policy resource includes the value of the policy identifier ({policyId}).
The status of the A1 policy is a property of the policy resources (i.e. the URI includes /status).
The PolicyObject transferred as content in the Create policy, Query policy and Update policy operations is a representation of
the A1 policy resource that represents the A1 policy enforcement activity in the Near-RT RIC.
The PolicyStatusObject transferred as content in the Notify policy status operation is a representation of the A1 policy status
and may contain feedback information.
ProblemDetails may be included in response messages with error codes. The current definition is based on free text fields and
mainly serve error handling during development and integration rather than enabling run-time corrections.
4.3.2
Operations and response codes
Create policy is defined as a PUT operation towards the URI including the policy identifier. The response code is 201 Created
if policy creation is accepted and enforcement status can be ENFORCED. If policy creation is rejected, an appropriate HTTP
status code is used to indicate the reject reason and Non-RT RIC could use it for making a new policy creation request.
Update policy is defined as a PUT operation towards the URI including the policy identifier. The response code is 200 OK if
policy update is accepted and enforcement status can be ENFORCED. If policy update is rejected, an appropriate HTTP stat

uest.
Update policy is defined as a PUT operation towards the URI including the policy identifier. The response code is 200 OK if
policy update is accepted and enforcement status can be ENFORCED. If policy update is rejected, an appropriate HTTP status
code is used to indicate the reject reason and Non-RT RIC could use it for making a new policy update request.
Delete policy is defined as a DELETE operation with a 204 No content response code. Policy deletion is not supposed to be
rejected although an appropriate error code could be used in such case.
Notify policy status is defined as a POST operation with a 204 No content response code. If policy status notification is
rejected, an appropriate HTTP status code is used to indicate the reject reason though Near-RT RIC is expected to use for
resending the notification.
NOTE:
The Query policy operations and Query policy status operations are not described here since not impacting A1
policy lifecycle management (in case status notifications are subscribed to).
4.4
A1 policy status and feedback
4.4.1
Policy status object
The PolicyStatusObject defined in A1TD [i.4] is used in three different use cases:
In Notify policy status change (see A1UCR [1.2], clause 6.7.3.2) the PolicyStatusObject includes enforceStatus (i.e. if the
enforcement status has become ENFORCED or NOT_ENFORCED) and enforceReason (i.e. indicating the reason for the
enforcement status change).
In Query policy status (see A1UCR [1.2], clause 6.7.3.1), the PolicyStatusObject includes enforceStatus (i.e. if the
enforcement status is ENFORCED or NOT_ENFORCED) and may include enforceReason (i.e. indicating the reason for the
latest enforcement status change).
In Notify policy feedback (not yet defined in A1UCR [1.2]), the PolicyStatusObject includes policy type s

rcement status is ENFORCED or NOT_ENFORCED) and may include enforceReason (i.e. indicating the reason for the
latest enforcement status change).
In Notify policy feedback (not yet defined in A1UCR [1.2]), the PolicyStatusObject includes policy type specific feedback
information in addition to enforceStatus (and enforceReason).

4.4.2
Enforcement status
The enforceStatus can take the values ENFORCED or NOT_ENFORCED.
NOTE:
An A1 policy can be ENFORCED even if the UEs identified through the scope of the A1 policy are not present
in any cell handled by the Near-RT RIC, i.e. even if there is no effect resulting from the enforcement activity in
the Near-RT RIC.
4.4.3
Change reasons
The enforceReason can take the values SCOPE_NOT_APPLICABLE or STATEMENT_NOT APPLICABLE or
OTHER_REASON.
The detailed meaning of “NOT_APPLICABLE” is currently not defined.
NOTE:
A proper definition of “NOT_APPLICABLE” could be used also as extension of ProblemDetails to provide
further details in a response message with an error code (e.g. to indicate a “rejectReason”).
4.4.4
Feedback
The feedback part of a PolicyStatusObject is policy type specific as defined by the policy status schema of each A1 policy type
(see A1TD [i.4], clauses 7.2).
NOTE:
Currently no policy type specific part of a status schema is defined for any policy type in A1TD [i.4]).
5
Enhanced descriptions of A1 policy enforcement
5.1
Introduction
This clause discusses A1 policy enforcement with enhanced descriptions that do not explicitly correspond to the current A1
specifications.
5.2
A1 policy structure and contents
5.2.1
Overview
An A1 policy can contain three parts – scope identifier, policy objectives statement, and policy resources statement (see
A1GAP [i.1], clause 5.1.5) – and can be read as expressing an instruction with the meaning:
For the entities identified in the scope, strive for achieving the objectives by utilizing the conditions expressed for the
resources.
The scope identifier defined in A1TD [i.4] enables explicit or implicit identification of UEs and cells for which the
enforcement aims to have an impact, and towards which the object

objectives by utilizing the conditions expressed for the
resources.
The scope identifier defined in A1TD [i.4] enables explicit or implicit identification of UEs and cells for which the
enforcement aims to have an impact, and towards which the objectives would be evaluated. A UE must be connected to an
identified cell to be impacted by policy enforcement.
5.2.2
Scope targets
To describe A1 policy enforcement, the entities being identified through the scope identifier in an A1 policy are in the present
document referred to as the scope targets.
The following attributes are currently defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 6.3.1 for the scope identifier: ueId, groupId, sliceId, qosId,
cellId, cellIdList, and taIList.
The scope targets enable identification of what is to be impacted (related to an observable outcome that can be expressed in the
objectives statement) and what the required A1 policy enforcement capabilities are (e.g. which cells and slices that must be
available for enforcing the policy).

5.2.3
Objectives
An A1 policy can contain one or more objectives. The current A1 specifications do not describe how to measure or evaluate
the degree to which the objectives are achieved, it is left for Non-RT RIC to determine to which extent A1 policy enforcement
leads to the intended result (see clause 4.1.2).
Several of the A1 policy types defined in A1TD [i.4] require "at least one" of several objective attributes to be present in an A1
policy.
NOTE:
Assumingly, not any combination of objectives attributes, and attribute values, may make sense from a
consistent enforcement perspective.
For specific objective attributes, not all attribute values may make sense. E.g. the policy schema may allow values that are
considered unreasonable from the Near-RT RIC perspective.
The current A1 specifications do not define any explicit error code or reject reason to use in case Near-RT RIC decides to
reject an A1 policy creation/update request for the above reasons.
Policy objectives may be unachievable due to conflicts with other policies or other tasks requiring the same resources in which
case rejection of a policy creation request would use the 409 Conflict status code, or due to required resources not being
available in which case a status change notification could indicate the change reason as OTHER REASON.
5.2.4
Resources
5.2.4.1
General considerations
The resource statements enabled by the A1 policy types currently defined in A1TD [i.4] are based on cells (i.e. cell lists) and
conditions related to their utilization for enforcing the A1 policy. While the cells in the scope need to be handled by the Near-
RT RIC which is enforcing the A1 policy, the cells in the resource statement need not be since traffic can be steered/off-loaded
to neighbouring cells handled by other Nea

ng the A1 policy. While the cells in the scope need to be handled by the Near-
RT RIC which is enforcing the A1 policy, the cells in the resource statement need not be since traffic can be steered/off-loaded
to neighbouring cells handled by other Near-RT RICs.
To transfer traffic to a cell (e.g. based on a traffic steering or a load balancing policy), a neighbourhood relation needs to be
configured and if such are not available the Near-RT RIC could consider the requested A1 policy as not applicable.
NOTE:
It is not studied in the present document if Near-RT RIC can be assumed to be aware of if the indicated cells
handled by other Near-RT RICs are available, or not, when evaluating the applicability of a requested A1 policy.
5.2.4.2
A1 Policy type specific considerations
5.2.4.2.1
Traffic steering preferences
Resource statements for traffic steering preferences are made based on the TspResource data type defined in A1TD [i.4],
clause 6.2.4.2.
The resource statement expresses conditions for cells to steer traffic to. It does not exclude usage of cells not included in the
cellLists in the resource statement.
The cells in the resource statement are not limited to cells handled by the Near-RT RIC.
5.2.4.2.2
Slice SLA assurance
Resource statements for slice SLA assurance are made based on the SliceSlaResources data type defined in A1TD [i.4], clause
6.2.4.3.
If present, the resource statement expresses the designated target cells for attributes in SliceSlaObjectives (see A1TD [i.4],
clause 6.3.3.5). It excludes usage of cells not included in the cellLists in the resource statement from being designated target
cells.
The cells in the resource statement are limited to cells handled by the Near-RT RIC.

5.2.4.2.3
Load balancing
Resource statements for load balancing are made based on the LbResources data type defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 6.2.4.4.
The resource statement expresses conditions for cells to transfer traffic to. It excludes usage of cells not included in the cellList
in the resource statement.
The cells in the resource statement are not limited to cells handled by the Near-RT RIC.
5.2.4.2.4
Energy saving
Resource statements for energy saving are made based on the EsResource data type defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 6.2.4.5.
The resource statements express conditions for cells to apply energy saving on. It does not exclude usage of cells not included
in the cellList in the resource statement.
The cells in the resource statement are limited to cells handled by the Near-RT RIC.
5.3
Applicability (from Near-RT RIC perspective)
5.3.1
Background
Applicability is currently used to express a reason for an A1 policy status change (see clause 4.4.3 and A1TD [i.4] clause
6.2.2.3). For the scope identifier, SCOPE_NOT_APPLICABLE implies one or more of the attributes of the scope identifier
cannot be applied, and hence the provided scope can no longer be applied for enforcing the A1 policy. For the objectives
statement, and the resource statement, STATEMENT_NOT_APPLICABLE implies the statement can no longer be applied.
Any detailed description of why the scope or the statements cannot be applied is currently not provided in the A1
specifications.
The term applicability could potentially also be used to express one of the reasons for why an A1 policy creation/update
request is rejected in a case when the requested A1 policy cannot be enforced. According to A1GAP [i.1], clause 5.1.3, Non-
RT RIC can when an A1 policy creation request is accepted assume that the A1 policy is

request is rejected in a case when the requested A1 policy cannot be enforced. According to A1GAP [i.1], clause 5.1.3, Non-
RT RIC can when an A1 policy creation request is accepted assume that the A1 policy is enforced. This means scope and

NOTE:
The current A1 specifications do not define any explicit error code or reject reason to use in case Near-RT RIC

the status code 400 Bad Request and optionally express the reasons in the problem details.
Knowledge about which A1 policies that are applicable from a Near-RT RIC perspective would help Non-RT RIC to formulate
A1 policies that can be enforced, and better understand reasons for why an existing A1 policy is not achieving its objectives.

A definition of the term applicability would, in general, relate to the capabilities needed for applying.
EXAMPLE 1:
A Near-RT RIC could consider an A1 policy as applicable in case it has capabilities, and is allowed to use
them, to enforce it while it would consider an A1 policy as not_applicable in case it does not have
capabilities, or is not allowed to use them, to enforce it.
For the A1 interface purposes, it could be considered for Near-RT RIC to express such A1 (policy enforcement) capabilities
related to the A1 policy types it supports.

For the A1 interface purposes, it could be considered for Near-RT RIC to express such A1 (policy enforcement) capabilities
related to the A1 policy types it supports.
The A1 policy enforcement capabilities of a Near-RT RIC could represent what the Near-RT RIC is able, and allowed, to do
in terms of A1 policy enforcement related to a supported A1 policy type. Based on its A1 policy enforcement capabilities, a
Near-RT RIC could consider a requested A1 policy as applicable or not applicable.

EXAMPLE 2:
If a Near-RT RIC has A1 policy enforcement capabilities to enforce A1 policies for cells 100-199, it
would not consider an A1 policy that targets cell 201 as fully applicable since it does not have all the
required A1 policy enforcement capabilities to enforce it. If Non-RT RIC was aware of these A1 policy
enforcement capabilities, it would (hopefully) not create an A1 policy that expects cell 201 to be used for
A1 policy enforcement.
Two aspects of A1 policy enforcement capabilities should be separated – "configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities" and
"available A1 policy enforcement capabilities":

the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities of a Near-RT RIC represents the capabilities configured by
OAM that the Near-RT RIC can, and is allowed to, use for A1 policy enforcement (e.g., each cell is handled by one
and only one Near-RT RIC based on the network configuration and cells are configured for support for certain slices);
and

the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities of a Near-RT RIC represents the subset of configured A1 policy
enforcement capabilities that are available for A1 policy enforcement (e.g., all the configured cells or slices may not
be available for enforcing A1 policies at every time).
Since the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities are a subset of the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities, they
may change in case the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities are changed. It is assumed that the available A1 policy
enforcement capabilities may change more often than the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities, but they can only
change within the set of configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
NOTE 1: The reasons for why configured cells or slices may not always be available for enforcemen

change within the set of configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
NOTE 1: The reasons for why configured cells or slices may not always be available for enforcement of A1 policies is not
further elaborated here.
NOTE 2: "Planned A1 policy enforcement capabilities" may not be relevant to consider. Only configured A1 policy
enforcement capabilities are relevant when defining applicability for a Near-RT RIC that receives A1 policy
creation/update requests and/or is enforcing A1 policies.
5.3.3
Scope applicability
5.3.3.1
Examples of A1 policy enforcement capabilities
In the context of the A1 interface, the obvious examples of A1 policy enforcement capabilities are those that can be
represented by the entities identified in the scope and resources statement (e.g. cells and slices), and the attributes of the
objectives statement, defined in the A1 policy types. The configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities represent the subset of
what can be expressed in A1 policies based on the A1 policy types that a Near-RT RIC has been configured or restricted to
support.
A Near-RT RIC can e.g. be configured with

restrictions to use only certain of the allowed combinations of scope identifier attributes with objectives/resources
statement defined for each A1 policy type;

restrictions to use only certain scope identifier attributes, i.e., Near-RT RIC can be configured to not allow
ueId/groupId/sliceId/qosId/cellId/cellIdList/talList based scope identifiers for an A1 policy type;

allowed or not allowed ueId/groupId/sliceId/qosId/cellId attributes, e.g., Near-RT RIC can be configured to not allow
qcI based scopes for a policy type;

allowed or not allowed scope identifier attribute values, e.g.,

fiers for an A1 policy type;

allowed or not allowed ueId/groupId/sliceId/qosId/cellId attributes, e.g., Near-RT RIC can be configured to not allow
qcI based scopes for a policy type;

allowed or not allowed scope identifier attribute values, e.g., Near-RT RIC can be configured to not allow A1 policy
enforcement for certain cellId(s) for an A1 policy type.
NOTE 1: Near-RT may be configured for A1 policy type restrictions as exemplified above given they are in line with the
A1 specifications. It is not in scope of the A1 specifications to define how cells are configured to support e.g.
slices and tracking areas, nor how Near-RT RIC is configured for restrictions or which cells it handles.

NOTE 2: In addition to the Near-RT RIC configuration, the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities could be
impacted by other aspects related to the internal realization of the Near-RT RIC. E.g., in case the A1 policy
enforcement would be distributed among activities that enforce a share of the A1 policy, the operational status of
those activities could impact the A1 policy enforcement capabilities that are available, and Near-RT RIC in such
a case could use the policy status message to indicate the change in the enforceability of the policy.
A Near-RT RIC would use its configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities to determine applicability of requested A1
policies (and use the available subset of the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities to determine enforceability of

The term applicability expresses if enforcement of an A1 policy can be based on the configured A1 policy enforcement

if the scope of an A1 policy is completely covered by the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities, it is
referred to as an "applicable scope"; and

if the scope of an A1 policy is not completely covered by the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities, it is
referred to as a "not applicable scope".

can be handled based on the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities;



NOTE:
If a cellIdList in the scope includes cells handled by other Near-RT RIC(s), obviously the requested scope is
bigger than, or outside of, the applicable scope. But when there is a ueId in a requested scope, and the Near-RT
RIC is configured to allow ueId based scope, then the requested scope can be an applicable scope.
The current A1 specifications do not make any assumptions on when Near-RT RIC evaluates the applicable scope and/or the
enforceable scope against the configured and/or available A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
5.3.4
Objectives applicability
If the enforcement status of an A1 policy changes to NOT_ENFORCED, the changeReason
STATEMENT_NOT_APPLICABLE could be used to indicate that the reason is related to that objectives can no longer be
applied. It can also be used in the case that an A1 policy update request was accepted although objectives are no longer
realistic or within the constraints.
An A1 policy creation/update request could potentially be rejected due to inapplicability in case the objectives are:
"unrealistic" or "beyond constraints".
The objectives statement of an A1 policy could be considered as applicable in case the policy creation/update request can be
accepted and the enforcement status of the A1 policy can be ENFORCED.
NOTE:
An A1 policy creation/update request can be rejected due to conflict in case the existence of other policies
implies the objectiv

se the policy creation/update request can be
accepted and the enforcement status of the A1 policy can be ENFORCED.
NOTE:
An A1 policy creation/update request can be rejected due to conflict in case the existence of other policies
implies the objectives are "unachievable". This is, though, not related to objective applicability since not related
to the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
It would be up to a Near-RT RIC if, and how, it can determine if the objectives statement of an A1 policy is unrealistic to an
extent that leads to rejection of an A1 policy creation/update request or if the A1 policy is accepted even if the objectives
statement may not be (always and fully) applicable.
Even for a less unrealistic objective, the Near-RT RIC may have constraints related to which objective attribute values it can
consider as applicable.
In addition to constraints regrading objective attribute values, a Near-RT RIC may for each A1 policy type also be restricted to
use only a subset of the attributes defined for the objectives statement, and/or a subset of combinations of them (in cases where
the A1 policy types allow for more than one objective attribute). Such constraints are considered as covered by the configured
A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
NOTE1 : If Non-RT RIC was aware of the ranges for attribute values that Near-RT RIC considers unrealistic, or beyond
constraints, it would (hopefully) not create an A1 policy with an objective that is not applicable.
NOTE 2: It needs, however, to be further studied if it makes sense to reject an A1 policy creation/update request based on
the dynamic situation or if that is better expressed as a status of the enforcement.
To a Near-RT RIC, the objectives statement in an A1 policy would be "applicable" in case it can

makes sense to reject an A1 policy creation/update request based on
the dynamic situation or if that is better expressed as a status of the enforcement.
To a Near-RT RIC, the objectives statement in an A1 policy would be "applicable" in case it can use the objective attributes for
enforcement of the A1 policy and the values of the objective attributes are reasonable (i.e. within the constraints of what can be
strived for during enforcement). In case an objectives statement contains multiple attributes, the objectives need to be
concurrently achievable (i.e. also the combination of attributes, and their values, can be used) if the A1 policy is to be
considered as "applicable".
5.3.5
Resources applicability
If the enforcement status of an A1 policy changes to NOT_ENFORCED, the changeReason
STATEMENT_NOT_APPLICABLE could be used to indicate that the reason is related to that the resources statement can no
longer be applied.
An A1 policy creation/update request could potentially be rejected due to inapplicability in case the provided resource
statement is not applicable.

The applicability of the resource statement would be related to the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities or
neighbourhood relations. For a cell identifier attribute provided in the resource statement to be applicable, it has to be covered
by the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities or neighbourhood relations for the resource statement to be applicable.
The entities in resource statements are cellIdList and taiList. Even if a valid A1 policy need not have any items in the arrays, a
resources statement would not be applicable in case it does not cover at least one applicable cell.
5.4
Enforceability (from Near-RT RIC perspective)
5.4.1
Background
Enforcement refers to the activity and actions that strive to achieve the objectives of an existing A1 policy. The status of the
enforcement activity is expressed in the enforceStatus attribute. To say an A1 policy is enforced corresponds to that the
enforceStatus attribute value is ENFORCED, and to say an A1 policy is not enforced corresponds to that the enforceStatus
attribute value is NOT_ENFORCED. An enforceable A1 policy has an enforceable scope (see clause 5.3.3.2) and can be
enforced.
A UE identified by the scope of an enforced A1 policy may, or may not, be connected to a cell handled by the Near-RT RIC.
And PDU sessions related to QoS flows identified by the scope of an enforced A1 policy may, or may not, be established with
a UE connected to a cell handled by the Near-RT RIC. To say an A1 policy is enforceable, or that enforceStatus is
ENFORCED, does not reflect whether enforcement is in effect or not. Policy enforcement would not be in effect if the targeted
UEs are not connected, or if no PDU session is established with a QoS flow for the targeted qosId. Only when policy
enforcement is in effect, for

lect whether enforcement is in effect or not. Policy enforcement would not be in effect if the targeted
UEs are not connected, or if no PDU session is established with a QoS flow for the targeted qosId. Only when policy
enforcement is in effect, for A1 policies with ueId and/or qosId in the scope, can there be an observable outcome.
5.4.2
Effect of policy enforcement
Policy enforcement relies on that the identified required resources are available, allocated, and used for enforcing the policy
towards achievement of the policy objectives.
NOTE 1: The scope of WG2 and the A1 specifications do not include how A1 policy enforcement is done by Near-RT
RIC, that is in scope for the Near-RT RIC Architecture [i.7] and other WG3 specifications. The present clause
only elaborates on aspects related to usage of the A1 interface from the Non-RT RIC perspective such as e.g.
observable effects of A1 policies created in a Near-RT RIC.
The enforcement of an A1 policy may have direct impact on UEs identified through the scope of the policy and indirect impact
on other UEs. For an A1 policy to have direct impact on a UE it needs to be connected to a cell where the policy is being
enforced.
EXAMPLE 1:
A load balancing or traffic steering policy has direct impact on UEs steered to other cells, and their
presence in the new cells may have impact on UEs already present there.
The enforcement of an A1 policy may or may not have effect on a UE, or result in an observable outcome, due to reasons such
as UE is not being connected or the UE mobility (where connections do not last long enough to show observable impact). The
effect of policy enforcement may also be impacted by dynamic aspects such as e.g. resource load and traffic situation. It may
not be feasible for the Near-RT RIC to determine a

where connections do not last long enough to show observable impact). The
effect of policy enforcement may also be impacted by dynamic aspects such as e.g. resource load and traffic situation. It may
not be feasible for the Near-RT RIC to determine and signal that the enforcement of an A1 policy has no effect.
If the policy objectives of a set of policies are not concurrently achievable, only a subset of the policies may have effect though
all policies are enforced.
EXAMPLE 2:
E.g. power saving on a cell may not be applied in case it is actively handling traffic.
An enforceable A1 policy targeting cells can be enforced only if the cells are available (i.e. operational), it would not be
enforceable otherwise. An energy saving policy is not considered as making a cell unavailable since it is for the Near-RT RIC
to balance the effect of concurrent policies towards the E2 nodes and the cells, and make the trade-off between power saving
and traffic handling.

NOTE 2: For the observable effects of A1 policies, Non-RT RIC relies on existing mechanisms such as O1 based
counters, trace etc to gather this information. It is not studied in the present document if it is feasible for the
Near-RT RIC to be aware of the connected state of all UEs targeted by an enforced A1 policy, especially in cases
when they move between cells and E2 nodes. Neither is it studied if there would be any reason to notify such
changes to Non-RT RIC.
5.4.3
Relation between enforceability and applicability
5.4.3.1
General
The terms applicability and enforceability are strongly related, could apply both during A1 policy creation/update transactions
and A1 policy enforcement, and could be defined based on A1 policy enforcement capabilities. They relate to the capabilities
needed for enforcement of an A1 policy of a specific A1 policy type, and enables expressing the result of an evaluation of if
the A1 policy can be enforced or not if created, as well as the enforcement status of an existing A1 policy.
5.4.3.2
Acceptable
An accepted A1 policy is an A1 policy that Near-RT RIC accepted for creation/update based on a requested A1 policy received
in an A1 policy creation/update message while a rejected A1 policy is a requested A1 policy that was not accepted for creation
due to reasons such as e.g. not valid or conflicting with existing A1 policies.
The current A1 specifications do not contain any additional requirements (beyond validity and not being identical to an
existing A1 policy) on when Near-RT RIC should consider a requested A1 policy as acceptable when receiving an A1 policy
creation/update request.
NOTE 1: If a requested A1 policy does not validate against the policy schema of the A1 policy type, the rejection is
indicated as a bad request. If a reque

as a conflict.
NOTE 2: It could be for further study if applicability and/or enforceability should be considered as further reject reasons.
5.4.3.3
Applicable and enforceable
An A1 policy would be "applicable" in case it has an applicable scope (see clause 5.3.3), and the objectives and resources
statements are applicable (see clauses 5.3.4 and 5.3.5). Otherwise, the A1 policy would be "not applicable".
A requested A1 policy could be "applicable" in case it has an applicable scope, and the objectives and resources statements are
applicable. If the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities change during enforcement so that the scope is no longer
completely covered by the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities, the policy would be "not_applicable".
An A1 policy would be "enforceable" in case it has an enforceable scope (see clause 5.3.3), the objectives statement is
applicable (see clauses 5.3.4), and at least one cell indicated in the resource statement is available. Otherwise, the A1 policy
would be "not enforceable".
A requested A1 policy could be "enforceable" in case it has an enforceable scope, the objectives statement is applicable, and at
least one cell indicated in the resource statement is available. If the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities change during
enforcement so that the scope is no longer completely covered by the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, the policy
would be "not_enforceable".

enforcement so that the scope is no longer completely covered by the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, the policy
would be "not_enforceable".
Since the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities are a subset of the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities, an
applicable A1 policy may or may not be enforceable, while an A1 policy that is not applicable also is not enforceable.

5.4.3.4
Reasons
In case of a change in enforcement status (from ENFORCED to NOT_ENFORCED), the enforceReason
SCOPE_NOT_APPLICABLE would be used to reflect a change in the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities required
for the enforcement.
The current A1 specifications does not contain any dedicated attribute value to express a status change to NOT_ENFORCED
related to that policy has become not_enforceable (i.e. due to a change in the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities
required for the enforcement).
NOTE:
It is not clear if the enforceReason STATEMENT_NOT_APPLICABLE could be used or not for expressing the
consequences of a change in the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
Even if the A1 policy at creation/update was considered as applicable based on the configured A1 policy enforcement
capabilities, it may not be enforced due the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities. The considerations in the present
clause are general and limited to binary states (able or not_able). The introduction of more granular "degrees of ability" is
made in further clauses.

A1 policy creation
5.5.1
General
The current A1 specification (see A1AP [i.3], clause 5.2.4.3) defines policy creation, and update, based on the PUT+201
pattern as illustrated in figure 5.5.1-1.

As per A1GAP [i.1], clause 5.1.3,
"A Create/Update policy request is accepted after the policy has been validated and considered as being possible to
enforce"
and
"When a create A1 policy request is accepted, the Non-RT RIC can assume that the policy is enforced until policy status is
queried or a change in enforcement status is notified".
NOTE 1: To say an A1 "policy is enforced" corresponds to that the enforceStatus attribute value is ENFORCED (see
clause 5.4.1) when enforcement actions are taken for the A1 policy. It could be considered if the text in A1GAP
[i.1] means to imply Non-RT RIC can assume policy enforcement has started (and enforcement status is
reflected in the enforceStatus attribute) following the confirmation that the requested A1 policy was considered
as possible to enforce.
NOTE 2: Based on the definitions and reasoning in clauses 5.4.3.3 and 5.4.3.4, it could be considered to say that a policy
is "possible to enforce" if it is applicable (and enforceable) as the changeReason values provided in status change
notifications refer to scope and statement inapplicability.
At reception of a 201 Created response message, Non-RT RIC is aware that the requested A1 policy has been validated and
considered as possible to enforce. It does, however, not yet know the value of the enforceStatus attribute or the status of the
enforcement activity that results from the accepted policy creation/update request. Hence, until it knows, Non-RT RIC can
reasonably assume the policy is enforced (since it is considered possible to enforce) and it may also assume that the value of
the enforceStatus attribute would be ENFORCED.

To become of aware the enforcement status, Non-RT RIC can query the policy status and subscribe to notifications for policy

The current definition of Create single policy reflects a synchronous design pattern as described in 3GPP TR 32.866 [i.9],
clause 7.5.6. A different alternative for defining a Create policy transaction would have been to use an asynchronous design
pattern as described in 3GPP TR 32.866 [i.9], clause 7.5.12. The PUT+202+Notify pattern would ensure Non-RT RIC receives
consistent information regarding status of evaluations and the resulting policy enforcement status in case policy creation was
accepted.
Using a design pattern with asynchronous properties implies the enforcement status can be explicitly provided and may, or
may not, allow for a NOT_ENFORCED outcome. The different alternatives based on these patterns are discussed further in
clauses 5.5.2 and 5.5.3 based on the principles that "an A1 policy is accepted for creation if it is possible to enforce" and "there
will be an enforcement activity with known status for an existing A1 policy", and with considerations how to avoid
assumptions.
The usage of different status codes related to the different evaluations (if policy is possible to enforce or not) are discussed in
clause 5.5.4.

Detailed analysis for PUT+201 pattern
5.5.2.1
General
To say an A1 policy is enforced corresponds to that the enforceStatus attribute value is ENFORCED (see clause 5.4.1) and
seems to imply that the policy enforcement (activity) has started. However, the statement that the "request is accepted after the
policy has been validated and considered as being possible to enforce" seems to imply that 201 Created can be sent after
evaluation of applicability and/or enforceability (see clauses 5.3 and 5.4) but before the policy enforcement (activ

ed after the
policy has been validated and considered as being possible to enforce" seems to imply that 201 Created can be sent after
evaluation of applicability and/or enforceability (see clauses 5.3 and 5.4) but before the policy enforcement (activity) has
started. Given that the enforceStatus is queryable after the 201 Created message, the attribute value may either reflect the status
of the ongoing enforcement activity or have a value assigned by Near-RT RIC that may, or may not, reflect the status of the
enforcement activity after it has been started.
The scenario where policy creation is accepted after the start of policy enforcement, and enforceStatus is known to be
ENFORCED at the reception of 201 Created, is described in clause 5.5.2.2 while the scenarios where policy creation is
accepted before the start of policy enforcement, and enforceStatus is assumed to be ENFORCED at the reception of 201
Created until queried, or a status change is notified, are described in clause 5.5.2.3.

This transaction for "creating an enforced policy" follows a synchronous design pattern as described in 3GPP TR 32.866 [i.9],

NOTE:
It is not in the scope of the A1 specifications to define any details on what the starting of a policy enforcement
activity covers, if it performed in steps, or how long it may take before it completes. Even if the PUT+201 based
transaction is considered as synchronous, Non-RT RIC cannot assume to be aware of the actual enforceStatus
within any specific time.
5.5.2.3 Creating policy before enforcement status is known
Figure 5.5.2.3-1 and figure 5.5.2.3-2 illustrate policy creation where the 201-messsage is sent before the enforcement activity
has started. In these scenarios, the policy is created even if the enforcement status may not be ENFORCED when enforcement
has started. Even if Non-RT RIC can assume the policy is enforced, it could, but may not, receive a status change notification
immediately after the 201-message.
These transactions formally separate the acceptance for creating the requested A1 policy from the status of the associated
enforcement activity. Thereby it allows for an outcome where the enforcement status is NOT_ENFORCED. Given that policy
creation is accepted only if the requested A1 policy is both applicable and enforceable, it would be reasonable to assume that
the enforcement status will be ENFORCED (corresponding to the assumption related to the current Create single policy
operation). It can, though, not be assumed that Near-RT RIC sets the initial value of enforceStatus to any specific value before
enforcement has started.

5.5.3
Alternatives based on PUT+202+Notify pattern
5.5.3.1
General
An alternative to using the PUT+201 pattern would be to use the PUT+202+Notify pattern. The meaning of the 202-response
message would be that "the creation request is accepted for evaluation, and the policy will be created if it is possible to
enforce".
The following Create policy transactions are based on Option 3 in 3GPP TR 32.866 [i.9], clause 7.5.12.
The scenario where policy is created when enforceStatus is known to be ENFORCED is described in clause 5.5.3.2 while the
scenario where policy is created irrespective of enforceStatus is described in clause 5.5.3.3.
The 202 Accepted message would contain a URI that enables to query the status of the ongoing evaluation activity. This status
would indicate if the "evaluation of the creation request, policy creation, and start of enforcement" activity is ongoing and
when completed the status would indicate if the result was that policy is created or not, and what the enforcement status is. The
status notification would also include the PolicyObject (just like the 201-response) and the PolicyStatusObject (reflecting the
known enforcement status).

Figure 5.5.3.2-1 illustrates policy creation after the enforcement activity has started and enforcement status is ENFORCED.

Comparison with PUT+201 pattern alternatives
The alternatives illustrated in figures 5.5.2.2-1 and 5.5.3.2-1 shows the A1 policy exists (and is queryable over A1) after the

expected that Near-RT RIC has this behaviour. A successful policy creation transaction always results in an A1 policy where
the enforcement status is ENFORCED.
The alternatives illustrated in figures 5.5.2.3-2 and 5.5.3.3-1 implies there is no need for Non-RT RIC to make any assumption
on the enforcement status at the creation of the A1 policy since it will be notified when the enforcement activity has started.
The 202-alternative is a

in figures 5.5.2.3-2 and 5.5.3.3-1 implies there is no need for Non-RT RIC to make any assumption
on the enforcement status at the creation of the A1 policy since it will be notified when the enforcement activity has started.
The 202-alternative is a typical pattern while the 201-alternative is a simpler solution based on the current service operation
modified for asynchronous properties. A successful policy creation transaction results in an A1 policy with known status, but a
consequence is that Non-RT RIC cannot expect an outcome where the enforcement status is ENFORCED when enforcement
activity has started (unless further means are taken to address the expectations on the outcome).
The alternative illustrated in figures 5.5.2.3-1 shows why Non-RT RIC should not make any assumptions on the enforcement
status at the creation of the A1 policy since it cannot have any expectation of what value Near-RT RIC will assign to the
enforceStatus attribute before the enforcement activity has started, and hence it cannot expect to be notified in case of a
specific status change from an assumed status. A successful policy creation transaction results in an A1 policy with unknown
status but if Non-RT RIC queries the status of the policy after creation it will become aware of the enforcement status even if
the enforcement activity has not yet started (in case it subscribes to policy status notifications). It will, however, not know
when the enforceStatus value reflects the status of the started enforcement activity.

5.5.4
Validations (by Near-RT RIC) and error codes
5.5.4.1
General
The transactions illustrated in clauses 5.5.2 and 5.5.3 start with a validation of the requested policy that also validates if "policy
is possible to enforce" in the 201 cases. In the cases when policy enforcement is started before policy creation is accepted, the
creation request can be rejected also in cases when the policy is possible to enforce. The usage of error codes is summarized in
figure 5.5.4.1-1.
The current A1 specification (see A1AP [i.3], clause 6.2.7.3) only defines HTTP status codes for cases where the policy
creation is rejected based on formal validation of the request syntax, the payload not validating against the policy schema, or
due to obvious conflict with an existing A1 policy. There is currently no explicit error code to use when rejecting a policy
creation request with reasons such "not applicable" or "not enforceable if created".
NOTE 1: "not applicable" and "not enforceable" are defined in clause 5.4.3.3.

Figure 5.5.4.1-1: Validations and error codes
NOTE 2: It is out of scope of the A1 specifications and the present document to speculate on, or specify how, Near-RT
RIC does internal evaluations of A1 policies and policy enforcement, or in which order such evaluations are
performed. This clause only intends to provide reasoning around appropriate HTTP status codes that could be
relevant in relation to the considerations and definitions of the present document.
5.5.4.2
Error codes for policy validation
For the syntactic validations,

400 Bad Request is used to indicate a bad request, e.g. invalid URI path or content that do not validate against the
required JSON schema;

404 Not Found is used to indicate that the policy type does not exist (i.e. there is no resource corresponding to the
{policyTypeId} in the path), and
in addition to the syntactic validation of the policy creation request message, additional aspects could be evaluated to address:




5.6
ACID properties of A1 policy transactions and enforcement
5.6.1
General
5.6.1.1
Background
According to Wikipedia [i.8]:

"In computer science, ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability) is a set of properties of database transactions
intended to guarantee data validity despite errors, power failures, and other mishaps. In the context of databases, a sequence
of database operations that satisfies the ACID properties ... is called a transaction."
and in short, it is described (in the context of database systems) that:

Atomicity guarantees that each transaction is treated as a single unit which either succeeds completely or fails
completely;

Consistency ensures that a transaction can only bring the system from one consistent system state to another;

Isolation ensures that concurrent execution of transactions leave the system in the same state that would have been
obtained if the transactions were executed sequentially, and

Durability guarantees that a committed transaction will remain committed even in the case of a system failure.
This clause (i.e. clause 5.6.1) introduces general (i.e. not database-related) wordings that enable discussion of ACID properties
of operations on a system that manage resources where a specific activity is performed related to each resource. These
wordings are then applied in clauses 5.6.2 and 5.6.3 for discussing the properties of A1 transactions and the A1 policy
enforcement activities related to A1 policies.
5.6.1.2
Transactions and activities
The general system considered here provides an interface for lifecycle management (i.e. create, update, and delete) of the
resources and their related activities, and for query and notification of activity status related. The transaction initiator can use
the interface to operate on the resource (and thereby implicitly on the related activity) while it cannot explicitly operate on the
activity. The tran

ities, and for query and notification of activity status related. The transaction initiator can use
the interface to operate on the resource (and thereby implicitly on the related activity) while it cannot explicitly operate on the
activity. The transaction initiator can create/update/delete a resource while the system handles the related activity and indicates
the activity status (i.e. if it is being performed or not). A successful create transaction results in a resource with a related
activity that is being performed, and a successful update transaction results in that the activity related to the updated resources
is being performed.
In the following,

the context is a system that handles resources based on create/update/delete transactions for which related activities
are performed when the resources exist;

the "effect of the transaction" is the created/update/deleted resource and the related activity being performed if the
resource exists;

the "state of the system" represents the existing resources and activities being performed, and is expressed based on
the state of the resources and the status of the activities;

the "state of the resource" represents the existence of a resource that have a resource URI that can be used to lifecycle
manage the resource and query the activity status; and

the "status of the activity" represents the activity being performed, or not, when the resource exists.
The ACID properties of transactions and activities are described in clause 5.6.1.4 based on the general ACID properties
described in clause 5.6.1.3.

NOTE:

transaction.

Isolation
Isolation would imply

the effect of transactions is independent of the order they are executed, and a transaction has no impact on the effect
of other transactions; and

an activity related to one resource can be performed irrespective of activities related to other resources.
NOTE:
This would imply a transaction cannot have impact on the activities created by previous transactions and an
ongoing activity cannot have impact on the handling of new transactions.

5.6.1.4
ACID properties of transactions and activities
The transactions defined in clause 5.6.1.2 show

atomicity property since a resource either exist, or do not exist after a transaction;

consistency property since the resource is being identified, and if information about the resource state, and changes to
it, is provided to the initiator of the transaction;

isolation property when related to different resources (while a delete transaction and an update transaction on the
same resource would not appear to be isolated); and

durability property if resources have the same state after restart or recovery as they had before.
The activities defined in clause 5.6.1.2 show

atomicity property since an activity related to an existing resource is either performed or not performed;

consistency property since an activity can be identified by the resource identifier, and if information about the activity
status, and changes to it, is provided to the initiator of the transaction;


isolation property for different activities (given they are related to different and unique resources and can be
performed independently); and

durability property if activity status is maintained after restart or recovery.
5.6.2

5.6.2.1
General
Referring to clause 5.6.1.2, the A1 policy is the resource being operated on using the A1 policy transactions and the activity is
the A1 policy enforcement activity related to an existing A1 policy.
An A1 Create/Update/Delete policy transaction consists of one request message and one response message, and additional
messages needed to convey the effect of the transaction (i.e. the resource state and the activity status) in case that is not
covered by the response message.

For the Create policy and Update policy transactions, an additional query or notification message may be needed to
inform the transaction initiator about the resource state (A1 policy exists or not) and/or the activity status (A1 policy
is enforced or not).

For the Delete policy transaction no additional message is needed since a successful deletion implies the A1 policy no
longer exist and, thus, no enforcement activity is no longer performed related to the A1 policy (that no longer exist).
While a Create policy transaction is being handled (i.e. after a Create policy transaction is initiated but before it is completed),
the A1 policy may not exist and the transaction itself would have the status of being "under evaluation". If the Create policy
transaction is handled stepwise so that the A1 policy is created before the enforcement status is determined, the enforcement
status would have the value "under evaluation" until the transaction is completed.

without the policy being created;

an Update policy transaction results in a policy remains existing after being updated, or not being updated; and


transactions since the lifecycle management responsibility is clear (i.e. creation, update, and deletion of A1 policies can only

5.6.3.1
General
Only an existing A1 policy can be enforced. The enforcement status is either ENFORCED or NOT_ENFORCED.
The enforcement status can be checked using the Query policy status procedure. When there is a change in enforcement status,
this can be notified using the Notify policy status procedure.

state or activity status. As described in A1GAP [i.1], clause 5.1.3 and figure 5.1.3-1, the Non-RT RIC view of
the activity status of the Near-RT RIC may be different if relying only on the Query policy status procedure than
if subscribing to status change notifications.

A partially enforced A1 policy (i.e. an A1 policy for which enforceStatus is PARTIALLY_ENFORCED) is an
existing A1 policy that is partly enforceable, and enforcement actions are taken for some parts of the A1 policy;

A not enforced A1 policy (i.e. an A1 policy for which enforceStatus is NOT_ENFORCED) is an existing A1 policy
that is not enforceable (or partly enforceable) or is not being enforced for other reasons.

6.2.5
Changes in A1 policy enforcement capabilities
Two scenarios can be distinguished related to how often A1 policy enforcement capabilities could change and what
consequences such changes may have on monitoring and lifecycle management of A1 policies:

In the first scenario, the normality is that the A1 policy enforcement capabilities available when an A1 policy was
created remains available for most A1 policy creations and during enforcement of the A1 policies, and


in the second scenario, the normality is that the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities change between A1
policy creations and during enforcement of an A1 policy.
For the first scenario, the enforceability can be full or partial while the achievability of the objectives could depend on which
of the A1 policy enforcement capabilities that are available.
For the second scenario, the achievability of the objectives may change, and the achievement may need to be evaluated, due
the changes in availability of the A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
In both scenarios,

detailed information regarding partial enforceability may be beneficial for monitoring and evaluation of the
achievement of the objectives of an enforced A1 policy; and

the enforceStatus and enforceReason attribute values give basic guidance for lifecycle management of A1 policies but
they may not be sufficient to guide the Non-RT RIC in all cases impacted by partiality. Detailed change information
including the partiality aspects could be valuable. This could be provided in the PolicyStatusObject that could be
based on a policy type specific status schema.
NOTE 1: For scenario 1, the detailed information regarding partial enforceability could be queried (since changes do not
occur often) while for scenario 2 it could also be provided in change notifications (since changes normally
occur).
NOTE 2: It is not studied in the present document if the detailed partiality information in a change notification would
cover all the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, or just the change of the available A1 policy
enforcement capabilities. If only the change (e.g. cell 135 not operational) is notified, the information of the
currently available A1 policy enforcement capabilities may need to be queryable

enforcement capabilities. If only the change (e.g. cell 135 not operational) is notified, the information of the

The enforceStatus and enforceReason attribute values, and the monitoring of the achievability of the objectives, enable the
Non-RT RIC to lifecycle manage its A1 policies.  The extended attributes values discussed in clause 6.2.3 and 6.2.4, and
detailed change information in PolicyStatusObject, could be beneficial in the presence of partiality. In either scenario, the
policy status notification could be sent whenever there is a change in partiality (assuming the notification content can be more
granular than the attribute value changes) and it would be clear for Non-RT RIC when policy status and A1 policy enforcement
capabilities may need to be queried, or policy status notifications could be expected.
6.3
Partiality scenarios
6.3.1
Introduction
This clause illustrates various scenarios that could occur depending on rules and conditions that have not yet been defined or
agreed. The scenarios are based on definitions and concepts illustrated in previous clauses in the present document.
Specifically, the definitions of A1 policy enforcement capabilities (see clause 5.3.2), acceptability (see clause 5.4.3.2),
applicability and enforceability (see clauses 5.4.3.3 and 6.2),  the enhanced descriptions of A1 transactions (see clause 5.5),
and the definitions of partial applicability and enforceability (see clause 6.2) are used for these partiality scenarios.
Partiality has effect on policy creation transactions and on policy enforcement activities. Aspects of partiality can result in
acceptance or rejection of a policy creation r

nd enforceability (see clause 6.2) are used for these partiality scenarios.
Partiality has effect on policy creation transactions and on policy enforcement activities. Aspects of partiality can result in
acceptance or rejection of a policy creation request, and impact the status of the policy enforcement activity for an existing A1
policy.
Partiality can be related to changes in the A1 policy enforcement capabilities where the configured A1 policy enforcement
capabilities may not change as often as the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities may do. Changes in the available A1
policy enforcement capabilities may impact an A1 policy enforcement activity and could be indicated in a policy status change
notification.
NOTE:
A change in the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities may imply a change to the available A1 policy
enforcement capabilities. It may be relevant to indicate in a policy status change notification if the change reason
is related also to the configured, or only to the available, A1 policy enforcement capabilities (see clause 6.2.4.3).
Information related to the configured, and available, A1 policy enforcement capabilities could be beneficial for the Non-RT
RIC to be aware of before initiating a policy creation transaction as they represent Near-RT RIC constraints for A1 policy
enforcement. Such constraints would indicate what expectations Non-RT RIC can have on the outcome of a policy creation

request and on the enforcement activity for an A1 policy, and awareness of such constraints would enable formulation of a
requested A1 policy that may be possible to enforce.
6.3.2
Policy type related constraints and status
6.3.2.1
General
As discussed in clause 5.3.3.1, the A1 policy enforcement capabilities are specific for a supported A1 policy type and could be
described based on the scope identifier attributes. The A1 policy enforcement capabilities represent the constraints for
requested A1 policies the Near-RT RIC would consider as applicable and/or enforceable.
NOTE:
If Near-RT RIC rejects policy creation requests based on such constraints, the constraints would provide an
indication of what Near-RT RIC considers as an acceptable/enforceable A1 policy. An accepted A1 policy
would then be "possible to enforce" is the sense that is applicable and/or enforceable.
The scope identifier can contain any values of the attributes (as defined by the common schema defined in A1TD [i.4], clause
7.1.2.1) and the constraints would express which values the Near-RT RIC can handle.
Constraints expressed by Near-RT RIC could also be related to supported attributes and attribute values ranges related to
objectives statements.
In case the constraints change, e.g. the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities are no longer the same as the configured
A1 policy enforcement capabilities, or none of the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities are currently available, the
Non-RT RIC could benefit from being notified.
6.3.2.2
Policy type constraints related to scope
The configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities represent what Near-RT RIC is configured for. The nodes and cells Near-
RT RIC can be handle would be part of the topology, and hence that information could be assumed

Other aspects of the Near-RT RIC configuration not related to topology, and the information of the available A1 policy

Scope identifier related constraints could be expressed using a generic constraints schema related to the common schema
defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 7.1.2.1.
6.3.2.3
Policy type constraints related to objectives
The A1 policy types defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 7.2, enables several combinations of attributes to be included in the
objectives statement of an A1 policy. If a Near-RT RIC does not support all attributes, or all combinations of supported
attributes, that can be expressed as constraints. Also, if Near-RT RIC considers certain attribute values as unreasonable or not
applicable, the supported attribute value ranges can be expressed as constraints.

policy type.
NOTE:
In the same way as EI job related constraints, see A1TD [i.4], clause 8.4.5.
6.3.2.4
Policy type constraints related to allowed combinations
In A1TD [i.4], clause 7.2, each policy type definition includes a table of the allowed combinations of scope identifier attributes
and objective statements. Just like a Near-RT RIC may not support all the specified objectives attributes, and not all
combinations of supported objective attributes, it may not support all the specified scope identifier attributes and thereby not
all the allowed combinations.
Constraints related to scope identifier attributes and allowed combinations could also be expressed as part of policy type
constraints.
6.3.2.5 Policy type status
In the same way as the status of an A1 policy enforcement activity is expressed as "policy status" using the enforceStatus
attribute, the status of the functionality related to enforcement of A1 policies of a certain A1 policy type can expressed as
"policy type status" using an attribute like e.g. opStatus.
Policy type status can be queried, and policy type status changes could be notified, over the A1 interface as illustrated in figure
6.3.2.5-1.
NOTE:
The use cases for policy type status are specified in A1UCR [i.2], clause 6.2.

Figure 6.3.2.5-1: Query policy type status and Notify policy type status operations
The opStatus attribute could have the following values:

OPERABLE if all the configured A1 enforcement capabilities are available;

INOPERABLE if none of the configured A1 enforcement capabilities are available; and

PART_OPERABLE if some, but not all, of the configured A1 enforcement capabilities are available.
The opStatus attribute values have some general relations with the enforceStatus attribute values for individual A1 policies
such that:

when policy type status is INOPERABLE, no A1 policy can be fully or partly enforced, and hence enforceStatus is
NOT_ENFORCED for all existing A1 policies;

when policy type status is OPERABLE, all existing A1 policies can be fully enforced, and hence enforceStatus can be
ENFORCED, but a specific A1 policy may be NOT_ENFORCED for other reasons; and

when policy type status is PART_OPERABLE, there is no general relation with enforceStatus of individual A1
policies as they can be either fully, partly, or not enforced depending on the extent to which their scope is covered by

the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, but a specific A1 policy may be NOT_ENFORCED for other
reasons.
The relation between policy type status changes and policy status changes for individual A1 policies would be depending the
general relations, as well as on which Case (see clause 6.2.3) is used for defining the meaning of the enforceStatus attribute
values, and this is further elaborated in clause 6.3.6.3.
6.3.3
Partiality and applicability
6.3.3.1
General
The partiality information related to applicability and enforceability could be expressed using the same attributes both when
considering constraints and change notifications. In both cases, content transferred over the A1 interface need to indicate if the
attributes apply to configured or to available A1 policy enforcement capabilities.
NOTE 1: When expressing constraints, the partiality information would contain the set of complete A1 policy enforcement
capabilities while for change notifications it is for further consideration if partiality information would be
expressed as the "complete capabilities" or only indicate the "capability change".
NOTE 2: It should be further considered if it is useful and reasonable to send a change notification for every change in the
available A1 policy enforcement capabilities during partial enforcement, or if it may cause extensive signalling
while providing minor value.
In case a policy creation request would be rejected due to partiality as discussed in clause 5.5.4.2, partiality information could
be provided in the response message that indicates the constraints-related reason for the reject. Alternatively, the error code of
the response message indicates that details can be retrieved by a query for constraints.
NOTE 3: When expressing a reject reason, it is for fur

nse message that indicates the constraints-related reason for the reject. Alternatively, the error code of
the response message indicates that details can be retrieved by a query for constraints.
NOTE 3: When expressing a reject reason, it is for further consideration if partiality information would be expressed as the
"current capabilities" or as the "missing capabilities".
6.3.3.2
Applicability
When receiving a policy creation request, the Near-RT RIC validates if it "possible to enforce" the requested A1 policy.
Assumingly this means Near-RT RIC would not accept the policy creation request if it does not have any of the required A1
policy enforcement capabilities, e.g. when the A1 policy is considered as "not applicable" or "not enforceable" at time of
evaluating the requested A1 policy (see clause 5.5).
Partial applicability covers a situation when the scope of an A1 policy is not completely covered by the configured A1 policy
enforcement capabilities. If a requested A1 policy considered as "partly applicable" was accepted, it would result in
ambiguities during policy enforcement since enforceability is only expressed related the applicable part of the scope of the
accepted A1 policy, i.e. the A1 policy could be considered as "fully enforceable" although the requested scope is not covered.
The current A1 specification does not exclude policy creation when the requested A1 policy has a "partly applicable scope" if
it has a "fully enforceable scope" (referring to the applicable part of the requested scope). For the present considerations on
partiality scenarios, "possible to enforce" implies the requested A1 policy is "applicable" and the policy creation request is
rejected (e.g. with the 501 code) in case the requested A1 policy is considered as "not applicable" or "

considerations on
partiality scenarios, "possible to enforce" implies the requested A1 policy is "applicable" and the policy creation request is
rejected (e.g. with the 501 code) in case the requested A1 policy is considered as "not applicable" or "partly applicable".
NOTE:
To be acceptable, the requested A1 policy must be a valid and (fully) applicable A1 policy. Near-RT RIC may,
though, reject a policy creation request for other reasons.
Non-RT RIC could use topology information or queried policy type constraints to formulate applicable A1 policies to avoid, or
as consequence of, rejection of policy creation requests with reject reason related to applicability.
6.3.4
Policy creation transactions
6.3.4.1
Enforceability
A successful A1 policy creation transaction results in creation of an A1 policy that is "possible to enforce" and for every
existing A1 policy there is an enforcement activity with known enforcement status.

NOTE1: Referring to the considerations in clause 5.5 and 6.3.3.2, the detailed principles for policy creation transactions
could be formulated "For a requested A1 policy to be created it has to be applicable" and "For an existing A1
policy, the enforceStatus has a value and there will be an enforcement activity, and after the enforcement activity
has started the enforceStatus attribute value reflects the status of the enforcement activity".
Partiality enables scenarios where the enforceability can be partial and may change during enforcement. In addition, partiality
needs to be considered during the evaluation of a policy creation request. Handling partiality during enforcement implies a
requested A1 policy could be accepted based on the applicability and enforceability validation without further conditions on
what the status of the enforcement activity is, or will be, after the creation of the A1 policy.
NOTE 2: Compared to the description in clause 5.5.2.2, this clause does not consider rejection of policy creation requests
in cases where the A1 policy would not be (fully) enforced after accepting the creation request. To be acceptable,
the requested A1 policy must be valid and (fully) applicable. It remains to be considered if acceptability also
could/should be related to if the requested A1 policy is considered as fully enforceable, or as fully or partly
enforceable.
NOTE 3: An approach where policy creation is accepted only if enforcement activity has started, and enforcement status is
"fully enforced", is covered by the transactions illustrated in figures 5.5.2.2-1 and 5.5.3.2-1 and is not further
considered in the present clause.

Different approaches exist for further interpreting "possible to enforce" in terms of enforceability when accepting a policy
creation request, e.g.:

Approach A: Policy creation is accepted only if the requested A1 policy is "fully enforceable". The value of the
enforceStatus attribute can then be ENFORCED when policy enforcement activity is started, or

Approach B: Policy creation is accepted if the requested A1 policy is "fully enforceable" or "partly enforceable". The
value of the enforceStatus attribute when starting policy enforcement would depend on which case (as defined in
clause 6.2.3) is applied.
Approach A implies it can be reasonable for Non-RT RIC to assumed that the A1 policy will be fully enforced after creation.
Given that it is possible for the A1 policy to be fully enforced after creation, it seems relevant to apply usage of the attribute

(and rather unexpected) outcome of the start of enforcement of a f

Assuming there is only one transaction specified for A1 policy creation (like the current PUT-based create policy operation),

Alternatively, several approaches and/or service operations could be specified and implemented if Non-RT RIC is enabled to
select one when requesting policy creation and thereby knows what outcome to expect and how it is indicated. One option for
enabling Non-RT RIC to select is to define different transactions and another option is to enable Non-RT RIC to express the
approach as part of the policy creation request.

If Approach A was specified using the PUT+201 pattern while Approach B was specified using the

6.3.5
Enforcement status changes
6.3.5.1
General
During policy enforcement, the degree of (partial) enforceability may change due to change in the available A1 policy
enforcement capabilities.
The enforceability may also change for other reasons such as e.g. lack of, or competition about, resources. In case those are
feasible to detect and handle, the impact could be indicated as a change in the partiality details of the enforcement.

When detecting a potential policy conflict, the re

feasible to detect and handle, the impact could be indicated as a change in the partiality details of the enforcement.

such a way that it implies a change in A1 policy enforcement capabilities available for the enforcement of
the existing policies and this may not result in any change in the achievability of the objectives.
Another aspect of partiality could be the degree of achievement of the policy objectives and resource usage. E.g. in case of a

how A1 policy enforcement capabilities are notified. It is not studied in the present document if, and how, partial
achievability of objectives can be indicated, and if it is meaningful.

Clause 6.2.3 defines cases that relates the enforceStatus to enforceability, and brings partiality into definitions of "enforced A1
policy". Based on these, and considering that an A1 policy may not be enforced for other reasons than implied by its
enforceability, the meaning of the enforceStatus attribute for the different cases can be defined as:
Case 1: If an A1 policy is fully enforceable, its enforcement status can be ENFORCED; and if it is partly enforceable or not
enforceable, its enforcement status is NOT_ENFORCED. The meaning of the enforceStatus attribute values can then be
expressed:

An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is ENFORCED is an existing A1 poli

enforceable, its enforcement status is NOT_ENFORCED. The meaning of the enforceStatus attribute values can then be


An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is ENFORCED is an existing A1 policy that is fully enforceable, and
enforcement actions are taken for all parts of the A1 policy;

An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is NOT_ENFORCED is an existing A1 policy that is not enforceable, or partly
enforceable, or is not being enforced for other reasons.
Case 2: If an A1 policy is fully enforceable or partly enforceable, its enforcement status can be ENFORCED; and if it is not
enforceable, its enforcement status is NOT_ENFORCED. The meaning of the enforceStatus attribute values can then be
expressed:

An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is ENFORCED is an existing A1 policy that is fully or partly enforceable, and
enforcement actions are taken for all or some parts of the A1 policy;


An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is NOT_ENFORCED is an existing A1 policy that is not enforceable or is not
being enforced for other reasons,
Case 3: If an A1 policy is fully enforceable, its enforcement status can be ENFORCED; if it is partly enforceable, its
enforcement status can be PARTIALLY_ENFORCED; and if it is not enforceable, its enforcement status is
NOT_ENFORCED. The meaning of the enforceStatus attribute values can then be expressed:

An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is ENFORCED is an existing A1 policy that is fully enforceable, and
enforcement actions are taken for all parts of the A1 policy;

An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is PARTIALLY_ENFORCED is an existing A1 policy that is partly
enforceable, and enforcement actions are taken for some parts of the A1 policy;

An A1 policy for which enforceStatus is NOT_ENFORCED is an existing A1 policy that is not enforceable or is not
being enforced for other reasons.

6.3.6.3.1 General
A change in status of the functionality related to enforcement of A1 policies of a certain type, caused by a change in the

6.3.6.3.2 Case specific considerations
Policy status and policy type status provide fundamental information for how Non-RT RIC could lifecycle manage an A1
policy by updating it, deleting it, or just waiting for some improvement in the availability of the A1 enforcement capabilities
(or resolution of other issues) under assumption that it will improve the achievability of the objectives.
The definition of policy type status is based on A1 policy enforcement capabilities and does not depend on how the
enforceStatus attributes values are defined and interpreted (see clause 6.3.5.2). The interpretation of enforceStatus, and policy
status changes, depend on the case used for defining the meaning of enforceStatus. The policy status changes may, or may not,
be correlated with a change in policy type status.
For Case 1, the policy type status complements the policy status for a specific A1 policy by indicating when the
NOT_ENFORCED status could indicate that enforcement actions may be taken for some parts of the A1 policy.
EXAMPLE 1:
Policy status is NOT_ENFORCED if the A1 policy is not enforceable. The policy status could be
NOT_ENFORCED if policy is partly enforceable, and if the policy type status is PART_OPERABLE, it
could be so that enforcement actions are taken (if a part of the scope is covered by the available A1 policy
enforcement capabilities) unless the policy is not being enforced for other reasons.
For Case 2, the policy type status complements the policy status for a specific A1 policy by indicating when the ENFORCED
status could indicate that enforcement actions are taken for some, rather than all, parts of the A1 policy.
EXAMPLE 2:
Policy status is ENFORCED if the A1 policy is fully enforceable unless the policy is not being enforced
for other reasons. The poli

6.5
Summary
The usage of the terms elaborated in clauses 5.3 and 5.4, and in the present clause, can be summarized as:
Requested A1 policy: the policy requested to be created/updated in an A1 policy creation/update request message
Requested scope: the scope in a requested A1 policy
NOTE 1: The requested scope may or may not be applicable
Valid A1 policy: a requested A1 policy that validates against the policy schema used by the Near-RT RIC
NOTE 2: The Non-RT RIC formulates the A1 policy based on the policy schema before requesting the A1 policy to be
created/updated, and the Near-RT RIC will validate the A1 policy against the policy schema when receiving the
A1 policy creation/update request. To say the A1 policy validates against the policy schema implies a validation
would be successful whenever it is performed and hence the A1 policy is considered as valid.
Accepted A1 policy: a requested A1 policy accepted to be created based on an A1 policy creation/update request message
NOTE 3: Term is used instead of saying "created policy" to avoid confusing the outcome of the creation process with the
long-term state of the A1 policy representing an enforcement activity

NOTE 4: To be acceptable, the requested A1 policy has to be a valid A1 policy and Near-RT RIC may also reject a
requested policy that it considers to be in conflict with an existing A1 policy.
Existing A1 policy: an A1 policy created/updated after accepting an A1 policy creation/update request message that has not
yet been deleted
NOTE 5: Term is used instead of saying "created policy" to avoid confusing the long-term state representing an
enforcement activity with the outcome of the creation process
Rejected A1 policy: an A1 policy not accepted to be created/updated based on an A1 policy creation/update request message
NOTE 6: The reject reason contained in the A1 policy creation/update response message could be used by the A1-P
Consumer to reformulate the requested A1 policy and can currently indicate if the requested A1 policy was
considered as “invalid” or "conflicting", and could in future cover other reasons such as e.g. "inapplicable",
"unachievable" etc
Applicability: expresses if enforcement of a valid A1 policy can be based on the configured A1 policy enforcement
capabilities and the supported objective attributes and their supported value ranges
An A1 policy would be

"not applicable" in case it has a not applicable scope, or the objectives statement is not applicable, or no part of the
resources statement is applicable; and

"partly applicable" otherwise


a "fully applicable scope" is completely covered;

An A1 policy would be
