20.3.1.3
Emergency wake-up procedure for TRX control
This clause describes the optional capability by which the O-RU's CU plane processing units and/or array elements
and/or other components that were put to sleep by a TRX Control command (or ASM command) can be woken up by
the NETCONF client as specified in O-RAN CUS plane specification [2], clause 16.11. The O-RU exposes this ability
to support emergency wake-up by including the leaf emergency-wake-up-command-supported in o-ran-module-
cap.yang YANG module.
A NETCONF client can send a <emergency-wake-up> RPC in order to wake-up the O-RU's CU plane processing units
and/or array elements and/or other components that have been put to sleep by a TRX Control command as illustrated in
Figure 20.3.1.3-1.
In the case of Shared O-RU (O-RUs that support the SHARED-ORU-MULTI-OPERATOR feature), only the Shared
O-RU Host can send a <emergency-wake-up> RPC which may include one or more optional sro-ids. Therefore, only
the CU plane processing units and/or array elements that are specific to the O-DU that is associated with the received
sro-id are woken-up. If sro-id is not included in the RPC, the O-RU shall wake-up all the CU plane processing units
and

efore, only
the CU plane processing units and/or array elements that are specific to the O-DU that is associated with the received
sro-id are woken-up. If sro-id is not included in the RPC, the O-RU shall wake-up all the CU plane processing units
and/or array elements irrespective of the O-DU.
Subsequently, a notification shall be sent by the O-RU to all subscribed O-DUs when the emergency wake-up
procedure is complete, after which the O-DUs may activate carriers (if needed) and then operate the C-Plane and U-
Plane to support user traffic. In the case of Shared O-RU (O-RUs that support the SHARED-ORU-MULTI-
OPERATOR feature), separate notification shall be sent for each sro-id received in the RPC.

20.3.1.4 Interaction with M-Plane processing
An O-RU supporting RF channel switch off/on for energy saving shall be able to disable C/U plane monitoring (see
clause 7.10). For example, an O-RU may support the cu-plane-monitoring container in its o-ran-supervision.yang
model, allowing an O-DU to disable C/U plane monitoring operation.
Operation of other M-plane procedures, including measuring of transport delay (clause 7.9), C/U plane transport
connectivity verification (clause 7.6) and O-RU synchronisation (clause 13) shall not be affected by network energy
savings functionality.
20.3.2
TRX control – M-Plane controlled
20.3.2.1
Introduction
TRX control via M-Plane messages is used to achieve energy saving through disabling one or more O-RU array
elements for an undefined period of time (until a next command is received). For example, an O-DU can switch off 32
out of 64 array elements of a massive MIMO antenna array. The TRX control capability and configuration are described
in clauses 20.3.2.2 and 20.3.2.3.
NOTE:
Clause 15.3.2 specifies another set of conditions allowing O-RU to save energy by disabling array
elements.
20.3.2.2
TRX control capability
The O-RU exposes the capability to support energy saving through disabling some or all of the O-RU’s antenna array
elements by including support of the feature MPLANE-TRX-CONTROL in its o-ran-wg4-features.yang YANG
module. If the feature is supported, then an O-RU controller can use the NETCONF session to recover the associated O-
RU TRX control capability information and parameters. These capability attributes are defined for each [tr]x-arrays.
These capabilities can be recovered by an O-RU controller at the O-RU start up as part of the o-ran-uplane-conf.yang
YANG module operations. The attributes are:
1)
mplane-trx-co

rameters. These capability attributes are defined for each [tr]x-arrays.
These capabilities can be recovered by an O-RU controller at the O-RU start up as part of the o-ran-uplane-conf.yang
YANG module operations. The attributes are:
1)
mplane-trx-control-txarr-capability-info: A container in o-ran-uplane-conf.yang YANG module with
capabilities that are specific to TRX Control for each tx-arrays. The parameters in the container include the
following:
-
mplane-trx-control-supp-antenna-masks: A grouping which contains the list mplane-supported-trx-
control-masks, which is a list of TRX control configurations that are supported by the O-RU which are
reported with their corresponding antenna-mask values. Refer to the O-RAN CUS plane specification
[2], clause 16.2 for more details on the usage of antenna masks. The absence of the list mplane-
supported-trx-control-masks indicates that any combination of antenna mask is supported by the O-RU
for a particular [tr]x-array.  If an antenna mask list is present, an all-ones antenna mask shall be included
in the list to assure all array elements can be turned on.
NOTE:
If the mplane-supported-trx-control-masks contains a single all-ones antenna mask, that means the
only valid antenna mask to configure is all array elements activated, meaning the TRX Control capability
is not present.
2)

capabilities that are specific to TRX Control for each rx-array. The parameters in the container include the
following:
-
mplane-trx-control-supp-antenna-masks: Same as this parameter description within mplane-trx-
control-txarr-capability-info above.
20.3.2.3
TRX control configuration
To support [tr]x-array level O-DU controlled antenna array configurat

he
following:
-
mplane-trx-control-supp-antenna-masks: Same as this parameter description within mplane-trx-
control-txarr-capability-info above.
20.3.2.3
TRX control configuration
To support [tr]x-array level O-DU controlled antenna array configuration, new O-RU level node array-config-group is
introduced. For M-Plane TRX control the node contains two lists tx-array-antenna-mask-config and rx-array-
antenna-mask-config, one each for specifying tx-array and rx-array configuration for TRX control respectively. The
list is indexed using array-name and contains parameters antenna-bitmask and antenna-bitmask-index. These two
parameters per tx-array and rx-array list entry may be used by the O-RU controller to perform TRX Control.  It is

252
problematic if TRX Control commands are issued for sub-arrays of a larger array due to the potential interaction of
multiple TRX Control commands affecting the same array elements which are part of multiple [tr]x-arrays.  Therefore,
the antenna mask configuration shall be done for the largest tx or rx array that is advertised by the O-RU, not for the tx-
array or rx-array which is a subset of the largest array (multiple non-overlapping largest arrays are possible).  The
effect of the configuration command shall be to impact the largest array (whether that largest array has any carriers
assigned to it or not).
For the case where the O-RU advertises mplane-supported-trx-control-masks list, RPC edit-config shall be used to
configure a specific antenna mask value by specifying a given antenna-bitmask-index for the [tr]x-array using the
YANG parameter [tr]x-array-antenna-mask-config .
EXAMPLE 1:
configuration of a given 32-bit tx antenna mask by specifying the antenna-index:
<tx-array-antenna-mask-config>
<array-name> tx-array-1 </array-name>
<antenna-bitmask-index> 1 </antenna-bitmask-index>
</tx-array-antenna-mask-config>
For the case where the O-RU does not advertise mplane-supported-trx-control-masks list for a given [tr]x-array, the
RPC edit-config shall be used to configure a specific antenna-bitmask value for the [tr]x-array using the YANG
parameter [tr]x-array-antenna-mask-config .
EXAMPLE 2:
configuration of a 32-bit tx antenna mask is shown below:
<tx-array-antenna-mask-config>
<array-name> tx-array-1 </array-name>
<antenna-bitmask >11111111000000000000000011111111</antenna-bitmask >
</tx-array-antenna-mask-config>

NOTE:
Binary values are encoded with a base-64 encoding (see reference [4]) so the above mask would actually
be represented as "/wAA/w==".
Prior to any M-Plane TRX Control antenna mask or associated antenna index being configured, the value of the antenna
mask shall be considered to be all-ones, meaning all array-elements are enabled.
Because updating an antenna mask via M-Plane is an asynchronous operation, the O-RU shall notify all notification
subscribers that the [tr]x-array specific commanded mask or antenna mask index has been implemented, using the
mplane-trx-control-ant-mask-update notification, as detailed in the Figure 20.3.2.3-1.

Figure 20.3.2.3-1 – TRX control configuration (M-Plane controlled)
To reduce unexpected transient related to the turning-off process, the O-DU may send zero-value beamforming weights
for any array element to be turned off prior to issuing the edit-config command turning off any array-elements, and may
keep them at zero-value while the array-elements are off.
To reduce unexpected transient related to the turning-on process, the O-DU may send zero-value beamforming weights
for any disabled array element to be turned on prior to issuing the edit-config command turning on the array-elements,
and may keep them at zero-value until receiving the notification that the new antenna mask activating those array
elements is received.
When TRX Control has disabled all array elements in a [tr]x-array, the O-RU may disable CU-Plane processing
associated with all array-carriers using that [tr]x-array, and the O-DU should assume that the CU-Plane processing for
those array-carrier has been halted by the O-RU.
20.3.2.4
Interaction with M-Plane processing
An O-RU supporting M-Plane controlled TRX Control for energy saving shall be able to disable C/U plane monitoring
(see clause 7.10). For example, an O-RU may support the cu-plane-monitoring container in its o-ran-supervision.yang
model, allowing an O-DU to disable C/U plane monitoring operation.
Operation of other M-plane procedures, including measuring of transport delay (clause 7.9), C/U plane transport
connectivity verification (clause 7.6) and O-RU synchronization (clause 13) shall not be affected by this network energy
savings feature’s functionality.
20.3.2.5
Interaction with C-Plane TRX Control and ASM
An O-DU using M-Plane TRX Control for energy saving shall be able to also use C-Plane TRX Control when an O-RU
supports both.  Howe

affected by this network energy
savings feature’s functionality.
20.3.2.5
Interaction with C-Plane TRX Control and ASM
An O-DU using M-Plane TRX Control for energy saving shall be able to also use C-Plane TRX Control when an O-RU
supports both.  However, the O-DU shall ensure the current M-Plane-commanded antenna mask (using antenna-mask
or antenna-index pointing to O-RU advertised supported antenna mask) is all-ones (all array elements active) prior to

254
issuing any C-Plane TRX Control commands, and the O-DU shall ensure the current C-Plane-commanded antenna
mask is all-ones (all array-elements active) prior to issuing any M-Plane TRX Control commands.
An O-DU using M-Plane TRX Control for energy saving shall be able to also use C-Plane ASM when an O-RU
supports both.  However, the O-DU shall ensure the current M-Plane-commanded antenna mask is all-ones (all array
elements active) prior to issuing any C-Plane ASM commands, and the O-DU shall ensure the current C-Plane-
commanded ASM conditions are terminated prior to issuing any M-Plane TRX Control commands.
NOTE:
The antenna mask is considered to be all-ones prior to any M-Plane or C-Plane TRX Control command
being issued.
20.3.3
Data layer control
20.3.3.1
Introduction
Data layer control is used to achieve energy saving through reducing the number of data layers independent of TRX-
Control. For example, the energy consumption of an O-RU can be reduced by turning off certain HW components like

processing requirements [i.6]. The methodology of data layer control using endpoint switch off/on is described in clause
20.3.3.2.

20.5
Deep-hibernate
20.5.1   Introduction
Deep-hibernate is an O-RU mode used to achieve relatively higher energy saving by disabling all carriers and stopping
the C/U/S/M functions and corresponding processing units when compared to power-state defined in clause 9.1.3 or
advanced sleep mode defined in clause 20.4.
20.5.2  Deep-hibernate module capabilities
The O-RU exposes its ability to support deep hibernate functionality by including support of the feature DEEP-
HIBERNATE in its o-ran-wg4-features.yang YANG module. The support of this feature means an O-RU shall
advertise the data node max-hibernate-time-duration and optionally advertise data node min-hibernate-time-
duration.
20.5.3  Configuration of deep-hibernate
This clause provides description of how deep-hibernate can be activated in the O-RU.
An O-RU Controller shall send an RPC <deep-hibernate> to activate the deep-hibernate in O-RU, which initiates the
corresponding timer. The RPC shall include the hibernate-time duration.
Before the O-DU sends the deep-hibernate RPC, the O-DU shall ensure that all [tr]x-array-carrier(s) shall be
deactivated as defined in Figure 15.3.2-0b. If an O-RU receives a deep-hibernate RPC while one or more [tr]x-array-
carriers are active, then it shall reject the RPC, including in the error-message the reason why deep-hibernation cannot
be activated.

257
If the deep-hibernate RPC is accepted by the O-RU, the O-RU shall cease processing control-plane, user-plane and
synchronization plane operations. If accepted, the O-RU shall send a notification to all subscribed O-RU Controllers to
indicate the deep-hibernate is activated, where the notification shall also indicate the hibernate-time. Upon receiving
notification from an O-RU, a subscribed O-RU Controller shall send the RPC <close-session> to the O-RU. The O-RU
shall suspend all NETCONF call home operations and/or PNF Registration operations after deep-hibernate mode
activated.
Once all NETCONF sessions are terminated, the M-Plane functions on O-RU shall then be stopped to reduce the further
energy consumption and O-RU enters deep-hibernate. The O-RU shall not respond to any incoming NETCONF session
while in deep-hibernate mode.
NOTE:
If any NETCONF session is not closed by NETCONF Client then the O-RU behavior is unspecified.
At the end of hibernate-time, the O-RU shall perform a re-start and follow the procedures defined in Figure 6.1-1.
Upon restart, the O-RU shall set the restart-cause to DEEP-HIBERNATE-RESTART using o-ran-operations.yang
YANG module. In case of autonomous O-RU restart while in deep-hibernate mode, e.g. because of some software
failure, the O-RU is not expected to continue the deep-hibernate mode.
In the case the O-RU is operating as a Shared O-RU as described in clause 19, an O-DU operating with "carrier"
privileges as defined in Table 6.5-1 shall be prohibited from sending the RPC <deep-hibernate>. How the Shared O-RU
Host coordinates with other O-DU(s) for the deep-hibernate activation is out of scope of the present document.

Maximum output power control
20.6.1  Introduction
Maximum output power control is an energy saving method used to reduce power consumption in O-RU. To achieve
this, the number of scheduled PRBs may be restricted by the O-DU, allowing the O-RU to adapt Power Amplifier (PA)
accordingly.
20.6.2 Maximum output power control capability
The O-RU exposes the capability to save energy through adjusting the maximum tx power by reporting support of the
feature MAX-POWER-CONTROL in its o-ran-wg4-features.yang YANG module. O-RU supporting MAX-
POWER-CONTROL reports capabilities using following YANG schema nodes:

each tx-array.
-
MAX-POWER-PER-TX-ARRAY-CARRIER-CONTROL: Enables the O-DU to configure the power
reduction for each tx-array-carrier.

20.6.3 Maximum output power control configuration
The maximum output power is controlled by the O-RU Controller through configuration of the max-power-level-index
parameter or carrier-max-power-reduction. The O-DU restricts the number of scheduled PRBs upper limit based on
network load or predictive analysis, with implementation specifics excluded from this document.
To control the maximum output power, the O-RU Controller shall configure the max-power-control-method value
according to the methods exposed by the O-RU in max-power-control-methods-supported, MAX-POWER-PER-
TX-ARRAY-CONTROL or MAX-POWER-PER-TX-ARRAY-CARRIER-CONTROL.
1)
If method MAX-POWER-PER-TX-ARRAY-CONTROL is selected: The O-DU may only configure the
max-power-level-index if the related tx-array reports supported-max-power-level. In this mode, the O-RU
controller should select and configure the leaf max-power-level-index per tx-array, then the O-RU calculates
and applies the corresponding level with array-max-power-reduction. The O-

that maximum power level that is scheduled to be transmitted at the tx-array is less than the configured

2)

21
Received power measurements for shared spectrum
bands
21.1
Introduction
There exists some spectrum that is designated as shared spectrum. To improve the sharing experience, received power
measurements can be beneficial in understanding the level to which the shared spectrum is being used. Citizens
Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) is an example of such a shared spectrum allocation, corresponding to 150MHz of
spectrum in the 3.5GHz band (3550 MHz to 3700 MHz) in the United States. CBRS band is lightly licensed and the use
is expected to reduce the cost of data transmissions. The CBRS architecture introduces the Spectrum Access System
(SAS) function that is responsible for authorisation and manages use of the shared spectrum [i.8]. To help inform the
SAS of the wireless environment, the O-RU can optionally support measurements of shared spectrum bands. An O-RU
supporting such optional capability shall include the o-ran-frequency-band-measurement model in its YANG library.
This clause 21 applies to O-RUs that support this optional capability.
NOTE:
This clause 21 defines the use of NETCONF-based procedures between an O-RU and an O-RU controller
for performing measurements of shared spectrum bands. Signalling between the O-RU Controller and the
SAS are out of scope of the present document.

261

An O-RU controller can use the received-power-measurement-request RPC to trigger the O-RU to start
measurements, as illustrated in Figure 21.2-1.





measurement points are NO_ARRAY, ONE_ARRAY and MULTIPLE_ARRAYS. Depending on the reported

with a single rx-array name provided (ONE_ARRAY) and/or with multiple rx-array names provided

controller shall configure the rx-array name(s) as the measurement point in the rx-array leaf-list in the

B.1.2
Statistics calculation
When configured by the NETCONF client, the O-RU captures the value of monitored parameters. Then the O-RU
calculates x = f(s), where f(s) is a function selected for specific statistics instance. The function f(s) can be one of the
following:
f(s) = s, if the function is set to RAW or function cannot be configured for the measurement-group
f(s) = LOG10(s), if the function is set to LOG_10
Where LOG10(s) is logarithm with base 10. To avoid issues with infinity, the O-RU assumes that for s < 10-128 value of
LOG10(s) is -128.
The value of x = f(s) is applied to first, latest, min and max values; related timestamps are also updated; frequency
table is updated as described in clause B.1.3.
When local measurement interval, which is not same as measurement-interval of the measurement-object, passes the
O-RU captures value of a monitored parameter (s). Then the O-RU calculates x = f(s), where f is a function selected for
specific parameter. The local measurement interval is up to the O-RU implementation matter and typically around 10
sec - 60 sec at earliest.
The value of x = f(s) is applied to latest value; related timestamp is updated.
The O-RU updates statistics:

If x < min value then x is applied to min value and related timestamp is updated.

If x > max value then x is applied to max value and related timestamp is updated.

Value of x is used to update frequency table as described in clause B.1.3 below.
After updates O-RU waits another interval to elapse.

________________________________________________________________________________________________
280
B.1.3
Frequency table generation
Let n = bin-count, a = lower-bound, b = upper-bound, x = f(s) where s is value of monitored parameter and f is a
function selected for statistics (selected via parameter function if it can be configured for a measurement-group and f(s)
= s otherwise, see also clause B.1.2).

If n = 0 then frequency table is empty and is not updated.

If n > 0 there are n bins: hk where k = 0...n-1. Initial value of each bin is zero (hk = 0 for k = 0...n-1).

If x < a then bin h0 is incremented.

If b ≤ x and n > 1 then bin hn-1 is incremented.

If a ≤ x and x < b and n > 2 then bin hk is incremented for k such that
-
k-1 ≤ (n-2) * (x-a) / (b-a) < k.
where the value of a bin should saturate at maximum without overflowing (the value is not incremented above
232-1).
Equivalently:
For k = 0, hk is a number of values x such that x < a.
For k = 1 ... n-2, hk is a number of values x such that
a + (b-a) * (k-1) / (n-2) ≤ x < a + (b-a) * (k) / (n-2).
For k = n-1, hk is a number of values x such that b ≤ x.
EXAMPLE:   function = LOG10, bin-count = 14, lower-bound = -12, upper-bound = 0
-
parameter value s = 0, x = f(0) = -128, -128 < -12 = a

h0 is incremented
-
parameter value s = 1e-12,
-
x = f(1e-12) = -12, (14 - 2) * (-12 - (-12)) / (0 - (-12)) = 12 * 0 / 12 < 1

h1 is incremented
-
parameter value s = 9,99e-12,
-
x = f(9.99e-12) = -11,0004, (14 - 2) * (-11,0004 - (-12)) / (0 - (-12)) = 12*0,9996 / 12 < 1

h1 is incremented
-
parameter value s = 1e-1,
-
x = f(1e-1) = -1, (14 - 2) * (-1 - (-12)) / (0 - (-12)) = 12 * 11 / 12 < 12

h12 is incremented
-
parameter value s = 1, x = f(1) = 0, 0 ≥ 0 = b

h13 is incremented

B.6

B.6.1
Statistics calculation
The symbol-rssi-stats is the time domain RSSI per symbol, the reference point for the TD-RSSI shall be the antenna
connector of the O-RU. The value of Received Signal Strength Indicator(RSSI) per rx-array-carrier per configured
OFDM symbol is measured. The RSSI shall be calculated as the linear average of the total received power observed in
the configured OFDM symbol in the measurement bandwidth from all sources including co-channel serving and non-
serving cells, adjacent channel interference, thermal noise, etc. over the total number of array elements of the array. The
unit of the reported RSSI is dBm.
If analogue or hybrid beamforming is enabled, the beamId used for RSSI measurement is:

When there is allocation of a beamId in this symbol, O-RU use that beamId for RSSI measurement.

When there is no allocation of a beamId in this symbol, it is up to O-RU implementation, for example, the O-
RU can choose to use a common beamId or use a previous allocated beamId.

F.1
Out of scope functionality
The present document does not include specific functions that, during the specification definition process, have been
highlighted as useful enhancements. The list of identified functionalities is shown below. This can be used to prioritize
future specification work within O-RAN Alliance.
1)
Beam Id field interpretation for various types of beamforming.
2)
Redundancy and failover scenario.
3)
Shared cell support for IP-defined flows.
4)
Enhancements to better align with O-RAN Alliance O1 specification.
5)
Shared cell topology discovery for architectures that do not ensure Ethernet frames sent between a south-node
and a north-node are bridged by an O-RU.
6)
Void.
7)
Dynamic sharing of O-RU carriers between multiple O-DUs.
8)
Enhanced adaptive delay operation that allows O-RU delay adaptation without requiring active carriers to be
disabled.
9)
The role of a Shared Resource Operator's SMO when operating with a multi-operator O-RU operated by a
third party Shared O-RU Host.

G.1
Model structure
In o-ran-lbm.yang model, the YANG structure is illustrated in Figure G-1:

Figure G-1: o-ran-lbm YANG structure
In contrast, the ieee-802-dot1q-cfm YANG  model has the structure illustrated in Figure G-2

Figure G-2: ieee-802-dot1q-cfm YANG structure
The ieee802-dot1q-cfm.yang model is not standalone model. It needs to be extended to work with ieee-dot1q-cfm-
bridge model or some equivalent. In o-ran-ieee802-dot1q-cfm.yang, interface and primary-vid are used to map to o-
ran-interfaces (where an l2vlan interface implicitly maps to an IEEE 802.1Q bridge equivalent).

________________________________________________________________________________________________
383
In both models, the maintenance association endpoint (mep) is mapped to a l2vlan interface (bridge interface) and the
l2vlan interface is mapped to a bridge equivalent. In the /cfm/maintenance-group/mep, interface and primary-vid
represents an ieee equivalent bridge instance. Association towards an ieee equivalent bridge is represented by parameter
on MEP in maintenance -group.
In o-ran-lbm.yang model,  remote-meps and maintenance-association-end-points are defined on the same level under
schema node component-list. Remote-meps contains MEP IDs that are in the MA but are located remotely (opposite
to local) and maintenance-association-endpoint contains mep configurations.
In ieee-802-dot1q-cfm model, information of meps is in two lists, maintenance-domain and maintenance-group.
The ieee-802-dot1q-cfm maintenance-association-mep list contains mep-ids for all configured meps that are in the
MA. The mep list in maintenance-group list has mep configurations for example mac address, enable parameter etc.
And in ieee-802-dot1q-cfm model, each mep contains a mep-db list used to store information of its remote-meps.  In
ieee-802-dot1q, if a maintenance-group is defined, remote MEP state machine is instantiated to all remote MEPs that
are presented in maintenance-association-mep list (that is active).
G.2
Mapping between models
To map the a o-ran-lbm.yang configuration to ieee-802-dot1q-cfm, the level of component which represent a bridge
will be mapped to ieee equivalent bridge instance which is represented by the combination of value interface and
primary-vid. The remote-meps leaf-list in o-ran-lbm.yang will be mapped to the maintenance-association-mep list in
ieee-802-dot1q-cf

To map the a o-ran-lbm.yang configuration to ieee-802-dot1q-cfm, maintenance-group will be generated for each MD,

10.3 File Management Operation: listAvailableFiles
10
This listAvailableFiles operation for the SMO is applied to obtain the available file list with files location and type from
11
the O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP by reading the AvailableFileList IOC as specified in O1 Interface Specification [3], clause
12
6.5.2. The listAvailableFiles operation for O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP can be performed independently.
13
10.4 File Management Operation: transferFile
14
The Transfer File Service provides the capability for the SMO to transfer files from or to the O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP.
15
SMO/OAM may perform this action as a result of a FileReady notification from the O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP informing
16
SMO that a file is now available to transfer. In any case, the file transfer is performed using a secure file transfer
17
protocol (SFTP or FTPeS) from or to the location provided by O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP. The SMO triggers file transfer
18
operation to O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP. Detailed procedure can be found in clause 6.5.3 of O1 Interface Specification [3].
19
The transferFile operation for O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP is performed independently.
20
10.5 File Management Operation: downloadFile
21
The Download File Service provides the capability for the SMO to request the O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP to download
22
the file(s) when the SMO has a file that needs to be downloaded. In any case, the file download is performed using a
23
secure file transfer protocol (SFTP or FTPeS) from the location provided by the SMO. The O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP
24
replies to the SMO with the result of the download procedure. Detailed procedure can be found in clause 6.5.4 of O1
25
Interface Specification [3]. The downloadFile operation for O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP is performed independently.

4.1.2 O1 interface for O-DU architecture model
22
O1 interface for O-DU is used for supporting the management features including “start up” installation, PNF software
23
management, provisioning management, performance management, fault management and file management towards the
24
O-DU.
25
The O1 interface for O-DU is also used to support O-RU management. For this purpose, specific models are used to
26
aggregate the configuration of individual O-RU functions (deployed as separate entities) and present them over the O1
27
interface of the O-DU(s) connected to them. The management of these O-RUs may be performed according to either
28
Hierarchical model or Hybrid model, depending on the particular deployment; see clause 12 for details regarding these
29
two models.
30

4.1.3 Transport Network
32
Based on the transport topology, various modes of network connectivity are possible between O-DU and O-CU and SMO.
33
The basic requirement for O1 interface for O-DU is to have end to end IP connectivity between the O-DU and the elements
34
managing it. The O-DU shall support either IPv4 or IPv6 and optionally support dual stack (IPv4 and IPv6).
35
This version of the O1 interface for O-DU has not been defined to be able to operate in the presence of any Network
36
Address Translation (NAT) between the O-DU and elements managing it.

1
O-RAN WG4 [2] specifies delay management between O-DU and O-RU, where transmission of data over fronthaul is
2
governed by O-DU transmission/reception window and O-RU transmission/reception window. O-RU
3

4
WG4 spec [2]. This clause addresses how O-DU transmission/reception window can be determined and the relevant
5
procedures and data models.
6

7
O-DU may support the following alternatives:
8
A) Not Configured by O1
9
➢
O-DU determines O-DU transmission/reception window. How O-DU determines the window is up to O-
10
DU, it may be hardcoded value at O-DU, or calculated from O-RU transmission/reception window and
11
FH delay based on O-RAN WG4 Management Plane Specification [2].

Configured by O1

10
15.2.2.1
Configuring O-RU general OAM related configuration
11
In hierarchical deployment, it is recommended that SMO configures general OAM related configuration for each Multi
12
O-DU O-RU using O1 toward only one sharing O-DU (primary). That O-DU then consequently uses the configuration
13
data to configure the Multi O-DU O-RU over its fronthaul interface. If SMO configures the same Multi O-DU O-RU
14
through more than one sharing O-DU, it is recommended that SMO validates outside of the O-DUs that the
15
configuration is aligned in all the sharing O-DUs to avoid configuration discrepancy. How validation is done is out of
16
the scope of the present document.
17
NOTE: O-RU does not check which O-DU(s) is configuring it, nor does it validate if e.g., same parameter is
18
configured to different allowed values by O-DUs.
19
In hybrid deployment, it is recommended that SMO directly configures all general OAM related configuration for each
20
Multi O-DU O-RU over its Fronthaul M-plane interface.
21
Refer to clause 12 for further details.
22

23
15.2.2.2
Managing O-RU general OAM related functions
24
In hierarchical deployment, it is recommended that SMO manages Multi O-DU O-RU general OAM functions using O1
25
toward only one sharing O-DU (primary), for example: software management, file Management, synchronization
26
aspects, antenna line devices, operational aspects of external IO, O-RU connectors, beamforming configuration update,
27
user account provisioning. If SMO manages general OAM functions for the same Multi O-DU O-RU through more than
28
one sharing O-DU, it is recommended that SMO co-ordinates the O-DUs that the management is aligned in all of the
29
sharing O-DUs to avoid discrepancy. How validation is done is out of the scope of the present document.
30
In hybrid deployment, it is recommended that SMO directly manages all Multi O-DU O-RU general OAM functions for
31
each Multi O-DU O-RU over its Fronthaul M-plane interface.
32
O-DUs may manage other O-RU functions independently e.g., NETCONF connection establishment, performance
33
management, fault management, static configuration for PRACH and SRS.
34
Refer to clause 12 and [2] clauses 8, 12, 13, 14.4, 14.5, 14.6, 15.4 for further details.
35

36
15.2.2.3
Configuring carrier configuration
37
SMO shall configure only the cells that the O-DU serves and their corresponding carriers over O1 towards that O-DU.
38
The O-DU shall then consequently configure the corresponding tx/rx-array-carriers on the Multi O-DU O-RUs over
39
their fronthaul interfaces.
40

41

46

15.2.2.4
Carrier state management
1
An O-DU shall only activate or deactivate the tx/rx-array-carriers on the Shared O-RU that belongs to the cells that the
2
O-DU serves.
3
When an O-DU receive a notification from a Shared O-RU indicating tx/rx-array-carrier state change, the O-DU shall
4
treat the notification in the same way as for a non-shared O-RU, i.e., O-DU shall ignore the notifications that do not
5
relate to the O-DU cell´s NRSectorCarriers.
6

7
15.2.3 Supervision Monitoring per O-DU
8
In hierarchical deployment, SMO may configure SecondaryODuInfo including attribute supervisionPerODu over O1 on
9
the primary O-DU. The primary O-DU shall then consequently configure Shared Resource Operator O-DU supervision
10
on each Shared O-RU.
11
In hybrid deployment, SMO instead may configure Shared Resource Operator O-DU supervision directly on each
12
Shared O-RU over its Fronthaul M-plane interface.
13
Refer to [2] clause 6.7, 19.3.4 for further details.
14

15
15.2.4 NETCONF call home
16
In hierarchical deployment, SMO may configure the SecondaryODuInfo including attribute callHomeClientInfo over
17
O1 only on the primary O-DU. If callHomeClientInfo has been configured, the primary O-DU shall then consequently
18
configure call home addresses on each Shared O-RU.
19
In hybrid deployment, SMO instead may configure call home addresses directly on each Shared O-RU over its
20
Fronthaul M-plane interface.
21

22
15.3 Multi Operator Shared O-RU
23
15.3.1 O-DU(s) roles
24
O-DU possible roles towards a Multi Operator Shared O-RU are defined in [2]. O-DU role towards all connected Multi
25
Operator Shared O-RUs is configured over O1 by setting oDuRoleOfSharedORu to one of the values:
26
“HOST_AND_SRO”, “HOST” or “SRO”.
27
When O-DU role is set to “HOST_AND_SRO”, the O-DU simultaneously perform the Shared O-RU Host role and the
28
Shared Resource Operator roles towards all connected Multi Operator Shared O-RUs.
29
When O-DU role is set to “HOST”, the O-DU only performs the Shared O-RU Host role, equaling Neutral Host. That
30
O-DU configures and manages all connected Multi Operator Shared O-RUs but does not have carriers in those O-RUs.
31
For each Multi Operator Shared O-RU, at most only one connected O-DU should perform the Shared O-RU Host role.
32
If no connected O-DU performs the Shared O-RU Host role, it is assumed that an SMO performs that role, acting as
33
Neutral Host. However, the scenario in which the Neutral Host is provided by SMO is not considered in this version of
34
the document.
35
In a hierarchical deployment containing Multi Operator Shared O-RUs, the O-DU performing the Shared O-RU Host
36
role uses the access control group “sudo” toward all connected Multi Operator Shared O-RUs. The O-DUs performing
37
only the Shared Resource Operator role (i.e., not together with the Shared O-RU Host role) use the access control group
38
“carrier” towards all connected Multi Operator Shared O-RUs.
39
In a hybrid deployment containing Multi Operator Shared O-RUs, if an O-DU performs the Shared O-RU Host role, it
40
uses the access control group “hybrid-odu” toward the Multi O-DU O-RU. The O-DUs performing only the Shared
41

47

Resource Operator role (i.e., not together with the Shared O-RU Host role) use the access control group “carrier”
1
towards all connected Multi Operator Shared O-RUs.
2
Following sub-clauses define what shall be configured over O1 to O-DU to realize O-DU functions defined in [2].
3

4
15.3.2 Configuring O-RU general OAM related configuration
5
In hierarchical deployment, it is recommended that SMO configures O-RU general OAM related configuration over O1
6
toward only the single Shared O-RU Host O-DU. The Shared O-RU Host O-DU shall then consequently configure
7
general OAM related configuration on the Multi Operator O-RUs over their fronthaul interfaces.
8
In hybrid deployment, it is recommended that SMO directly configures general OAM related configuration for each
9
Multi O-DU O-RU over its Fronthaul M-plane interface.
10

11
15.3.3 Managing O-RU general OAM related functions
12
In hierarchical deployment, it is recommended that SMO manages O-RU general OAM related functions over O1
13
toward only the single shared O-RU Host O-DU. The Shared O-RU Host O-DU shall then consequently manage
14
general OAM related functions on the Multi Operator O-RUs over their fronthaul interfaces.
15
In hybrid deployment, it is recommended that SMO directly manages Multi O-DU O-RU general OAM functions for
16
each Multi O-DU O-RU over its Fronthaul M-plane interface.
17

18
15.3.4 NETCONF server user account provisioning for shared resource
19
operators
20
In hierarchical deployment, SMO shall configure the SecondaryODuInfo over O1 only on the Shared O-RU Host O-
21
DU. The Shared O-RU Host O-DU shall then consequently configure Shared Resource Operator user accounts with
22
“carrier” access privilege and sro-id=sharedResourceOperatorId on the connected Multi Operator O-RUs over their
23
fronthaul interfaces.
24
NOTE: Value of each sharedResourceOperatorId shall be unique and associated with a particular Shared Resource
25
Operator only.
26
In hybrid deployment, SMO instead configures Shared Resource Operator user accounts with “carrier” access privilege
27
and sro-id=sharedResourceOperatorId directly on each Multi Operator O-RU over its Fronthaul M-plane interface.
28
Refer to [2] clause 19.3.1 for further details.
29

30
15.3.5 NETCONF call home
31
In hierarchical deployment, SMO may configure the SecondaryODuInfo including attribute callHomeClientInfo over
32
O1 only on the Shared O-RU Host O-DU. If callHomeClientInfo has been configured, the Shared O-RU Host O-DU
33
shall then consequently configure call home addresses on each Shared O-RU.
34
In hybrid deployment, SMO instead may configure call home addresses directly on each Shared O-RU using its
35
Fronthaul M-plane interface.
36
Refer to [2] clause 19.3.2 for further details.
37

38

48

15.3.6 Enhanced sro-id based NETCONF access control
1
SMO shall configure the attribute sharedResourceOperatorId over O1 with a unique value on each Shared Resource
2
Operator O-DU. The Shared Resource Operator O-DU shall then consequently use the value of
3
sharedResourceOperatorId for the user account of the NETCONF client with sro-id configured on the Multi Operator
4
Shared O-RUs.
5
Refer to [2] clause 19.3.3 for further details.
6

7
15.3.7 Supervision Monitoring per O-DU
8
In hierarchical deployment, SMO may configure SecondaryODuInfo including attribute supervisionPerODu over O1 on
9
the Shared O-RU Host. The Shared O-RU Host shall then consequently configure Shared Resource Operator O-DU
10
supervision on each Shared O-RU.
11
In hybrid deployment, SMO instead may configure Shared Resource Operator O-DU supervision directly on each
12
Shared O-RU using its Fronthaul M-plane interface.
13
Refer to [2] clause 6.7, 19.3.4 for further details.
14

15
15.3.8 Processing element configuration
16
Shared O-RU Host O-DU shall use the value of each Shared Resource Operator O-DUs sharedResourceOperatorId
17
attribute to configure a particular O-RU´s ru-element list entry as being uniquely associated with a particular Shared
18
Resource Operator. Shared O-RU Host O-DU gets sharedResourceOperatorId as defined in 13.3.6.
19
Refer to [2] clause 19.4.2.
20

21
15.3.9 Carrier Partitioning and Configuration in Shared O-RU
22
Only Shared O-RU Host O-DU has access privileges over Fronthaul M-plane to create tx/rx-array-carrier configuration
23
in the Shared O-RU.
24
NOTE: How Shared Resource Operators agree configuration partitioning is outside the scope of the present
25
document. It is assumed that operators mutually agree partitioning.
26
NOTE: How Shared Resource Operators configurations are validated is outside the scope of the present document.
27
It is assumed that operators mutually validate as part of configuration partitioning.
28
NOTE: How Shared Resource Operators agree eAxC-IDs partitioning is out of the scope of the present document. It
29
is assumed that operators mutually agree partitioning.
30
Refer to clause 12.1 and [2] clause 19.6.1, 19.11.
31

32
15.3.10 Notification of configuration updates
33
A Shared Resource Operator O-DU may configure subscriptions to receive notifications of modifications to a connected
34
shared O-RU’s datastore, according to the defined NETCONF access control privileges for the NETCONF client of that
35
Shared Resource Operator.
36
Refer to clause 12 and [2] clause 19.6.2 for further details.
37

17 O-DU behavior for 3GPP conformance testing
2
17.1 Introduction
3
This clause describes O-DU behavior to evaluate O-RU performance based on the 3GPP standardized conformance
4
tests.
5
To guarantee the minimum performance of gNB, O-RAN WG5 follows tests definition from [16], [17], and [18].
6
Any points not mentioned in this clause are expected to be in accordance with the corresponding test specifications in
7
[16], [17], and [18].
8
Note: The present version of this specification considers only PNF-deployed O-DU.
9
17.2 O-DU behavior for O-RU uplink evaluation
10
O-DU behavior for uplink tests specified in clauses 7 and 8 in [18] is as follows:
11
Step 1: O-DU receives a request, by O1, to conduct a test with the configuration parameters defined in Table 12 of
12
Annex E.
13
Step 2: In the test mode, when receiving signals from O-RU for a certain measurement period, O-DU counts
14
measurements shown in Table 12 of Annex E.
15
Step 3: O-DU reports the measurements results by O1 as PM counters specified in Annex A. After finishing reporting,
16
O-DU exits the test mode.
17
Note: A test of “Receiver spurious emissions” defined in clause 7.6 in [18] is not applicable to the above steps as it is
18
not measured at the O-DU.
19
17.3 O-DU behavior for O-RU downlink evaluation
20
O-DU behavior for downlink tests specified in clause 6 in [18] is as follows:
21
Step 1: O-DU receives a request, by O1, to conduct a test with the configuration parameters defined in Table 13 of
22
Annex E.
23
Step 2: In the test mode, O-DU generates test data and sends it to O-RU over CU-Plane of the Open Fronthaul interface.
24
After sending test data, the O-DU exits the test mode.
25
Note: O-DU doesn’t measure parameters in downlink tests because test results will be collected by the measurem

24
After sending test data, the O-DU exits the test mode.
25
Note: O-DU doesn’t measure parameters in downlink tests because test results will be collected by the measurement
26
equipment such as a spectrum analyzer.

power of only the antenna ports used to create Rx beam.

SI (Status Inspection)

round(x/y, 2) * 102, where:

PUSCH whenever PUSCH reception is expected when SSB used
for PUSCH is group of subcounter.SSB. The power is normalized
by PRB and antenna port. If Rx beam is created by some antenna
ports, this counter is calculated with the power of only the antenna
ports used to create Rx beam.
y is incremented by 1 whenever PUSCH reception is expected when
SSB used for PUSCH is group of subcounter.SSB.

maximum/minimum number of round(z, 2) * 102 . It is assigned
whenever z is updated by the volume round(z, 2) * 102, if round(z, 2) *
102 is bigger/smaller than previously counted volume, where:

PUSCH reception is expected when SSB used for PUSCH is group of
subcounter.SSB. The power is normalized by PRB and antenna port. If
Rx beam is created by some antenna ports, this counter is calculated

4.2.3.3 IPsec

4.2.3.3.1 Overview
5
The security of the F1/W1/E1/X2/Xn - interface control, user, synchronization and management plane
6
protocols is increased by providing encryption, integrity protection and communication peer authentication
7
with IPsec according [39]. IPSec can be applied to all IP traffic. It is possible to enable / disable IPsec and to
8
configure IPsec connections to peer-entities independently in terms of security settings for each remote IPsec
9
peer, e.g. per neighbor node or per plane. Further, it is possible to define connections to remote peers which
10
shall not be covered by IPsec although IPsec is enabled (bypassing traffic).
11
The supported IPsec capabilities follow [40] for interworking purposes and further appliance rules given in
12
[41], [42], [38] and [43]. Since IPsec standards include a high number of selectable security parameters
13
options, 3GPP has recommended to cut down the number of these options in order to guarantee
14
interoperability between different security domains.

Configuration Parameters
4.1
Parameter Name and Description
4.1.1
TimingList
This is a list of timing information for the self and peer O-DUs. First entry in the list contains information for the O-DU where
configuration is done. All other entries shall be set as per the peer O-DUs information. Order in this list shall be same as the
D2-c IP Address and SCTP port Num as defined in clause 4.1.5.
4.1.1.1
T1
This parameter as shown in Figure 4, with reference to a given OTA slot, indicates the minimum time required by SCell O-DU
to process and transmit data to a UE once data is received from PCell O-DU on D2 interface. It is defined in microseconds. If
the DL DATA TRANSFER and PUCCH RESOURCE TRANSFER for a given OTA slot arrives later than this time, SCell O-
DU may not transmit the data to the UE in the OTA indicated.
4.1.1.2
T2
This parameter as shown in Figure 4, with reference to a given OTA slot in DL DATA REQUIRED message, indicates the
minimum time required by PCell O-DU to process and respond to DL DATA REQUIRED message, and subsequent
transmission of data in the OTA slot. It is defined in microseconds. If PCell O-DU receives the DL DATA REQUIRED
message later than T2 time, it returns failure to SCell O-DU in PUCCH RESOURCE TRANSFER message.
4.1.1.3
T3
This parameter as shown in Figure 4, indicates the latest time by which pO-DU may send a DL SCHEDULING REQUEST
message requesting scheduling for a given OTA slot. It is defined in microseconds. If DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message
contains slot range lesser than T3, sO-DU shall ignore the received DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message. sO-DU shall
consider the slots that are greater than T3 as valid slots for scheduling the UEs.

This is a configuration list defines the IP address and SCTP port number for the D2-c interface of local O-DU and its peer O-

These parameters define the configuration of the IP address and UDP port number used for establishing the D2-u interface.

numbers to support multiple endpoints.

4.1.7 T_clearTB
This parameter specifies the maximum duration for which the SCell O-DU retains the transport Block (TB) for retransmission
following a HARQ failure. The timer is reset when the SCell O-DU receives a DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message
indicating retransmission request. Once the timer expires, the HARQ process becomes available for a new transmission, with
the NDI bit toggled.

1 Scope
1
The present document provides profiles for C-plane procedures and functions to achieve interoperability among different
2
vendors. The profile specifies the expected behavior of each node, e.g., message flow of each use case, definitions of IEs,
3
etc. which is not specified in 3GPP specifications. The profile specification provided in this document does not violate
4
3GPP specifications.
5
The use cases in this specification cover selected 3GPP functionalities.
6
In the IE tables:
7
-
If optional IEs are essential for a use case to work, they are categorized ‘included’ in the IE tables.
8
-
If optional IEs are used under certain conditions applicable for this use case, they are categorized ‘optionally
9
included’.
10
-
If optional IEs are not essential for the use case, they are set to ‘not included’.

One or more use cases described in this document can be initiated in a single procedure if this is allowed by 3GPP

specifications. In these cases, the IE tables need to be augmented and the ‘included’ IEs of the procedure are the

combination of ‘included’ IEs of the individual use cases, unless otherwise specified in 3GPP.

In addition, it is also possible to combine the initiation of one or multiple use cases of this document with other functions
16
of the 3GPP procedure as defined in the relevant 3GPP specifications.

3  Definition of terms, symbols and abbreviations
3.1 Terms
For the purposes of the present document, the terms given in [i.1] and the following apply:
carrier aggregation: aggregation of two or more NR or E-UTRA component carriers in order to support wider transmission
bandwidths
PCell O-DU:  O-DU, where the PCell is configured for a UE to support inter O-DU carrier aggregation.
pO-DU:  O-DU, where the PCell is configured for a UE to support inter O-DU carrier aggregation. This is same as PCell O-
DU used in the D2 GAP specifications.
SCell O-DU:  O-DU, where only SCell(s) are configured for a UE to support inter O-DU carrier aggregation.
sO-DU:  O-DU, where only SCell(s) are configured for a UE to support inter O-DU carrier aggregation. This is same as SCell
O-DU used in the D2 GAP specifications.
Elementary Procedure: D2CP consists of Elementary Procedures (EPs). An Elementary Procedure is a unit of interaction
between the O-DUs. These Elementary Procedures are defined separately and are intended to be used to build up complete
sequences in a flexible manner. If the independence between some EPs is restricted, it is described under the relevant EP
description. Unless otherwise stated by the restrictions, the EPs may be invoked independently of each other as standalone
procedures, which can be active in parallel. An EP consists of an initiating message and  possibly a response message.

Two kinds of EPs are used:
-
Class 1: Elementary Procedures with response (success and/or failure).
-
Class 2: Elementary Procedures without response.
For Class 1 EPs, the types of responses can be as follows:
Successful:

7

- A signaling message explicitly indicates that the elementary procedure successfully completed with the receipt of the
response.
Unsuccessful:
- A signaling message explicitly indicates that the EP failed.
- On time supervision expiry (i.e., absence of expected response).
Successful and Unsuccessful:
- One signaling message reports both a successful and unsuccessful outcome for the different included requests. The
response message used is the one defined for successful outcome.
Class 2 EPs are considered always successful.

4 Interface principles and characteristics

4.1 Procedure specification principles

The principle for specifying the procedure logic is to specify the functional behaviour of the terminating node exactly and
completely. Any rule that specifies the behaviour of the originating node shall be possible to be verified with information that
is visible within the system.
The following specification principles have been applied for the procedure text in clause 5.3
-
The procedure text discriminates between:
1) Functionality which "shall" be executed
The procedure text indicates that the receiving node "shall" perform a certain function Y under a certain condition. If the
receiving node supports procedure X but cannot perform functionality Y requested in the initiating message of a Class 1 EP,
the receiving node shall respond with the message used to report unsuccessful outcome for this procedure, containing an
appropriate cause value.
2) Functionality which "shall, if supported" be executed
The procedure text indicates that the receiving node "shall, if supported," perform a certain function Y under a certain
condition. If the receiving node supports procedure X, but does not support functionality Y, the receiving node shall proceed
with the execution of the EP, possibly informing the requesting node about the not supported functionality.
-
Any required inclusion of an optional IE in a response message is explicitly indicated in the procedure text. If the procedure
text does not explicitly indicate that an optional IE shall be included in a response message, the optional IE shall not be
included.

4.2 Forwards and backwards compatibility
The forward and backward compatibility of the D2CP protocol is assured by a mechanism where all current and future
messages, and IEs or groups of related IEs, include ID and criticality fields that are coded in a standard format that will not be
changed in the future. These parts can always be decoded regardless of the standard version.
For D2UP protocol extension fields are added in the messages to support forward and backward compatibility.

4.3 Specification notations
For the purposes of the present document, the following notations apply:

Procedure

When referring to an elementary procedure in the specification the Procedure Name is written with
the first letters in each word in upper case characters followed by the word "procedure", e.g.
D2 Setup procedure.

Message

When referring to a message in the specification the MESSAGE NAME is written with all letters
in upper case characters followed by the word "message", e.g. D2 SETUP REQUEST message.

IE

When referring to an information element (IE) in the specification the Information Element Name
is written with the first letters in each word in upper case characters and all letters in Italic font

followed by the abbreviation "IE", e.g. D2 UE ID IE.

Value of an IE  When referring to the value of an information element (IE) in the specification the "Value" is
written as it is specified in the specification enclosed by quotation marks, e.g. "Value".
5 D2 Control Plane protocol
5.1 D2CP services
D2CP provides the signalling services between the peer O-DUs which are required to fulfil the D2CP functions described in
clause 5.2. D2CP services are divided into two groups:

Non UE-associated services:
They are related to the whole D2 interface instance between the O-DUs utilising a non UE-
associated signalling connection.

UE-associated services:
They are related to a UE. D2CP functions that provide these services are associated with a
UE-associated signalling connection that is maintained for the UEs in question.

Unless explicitly indicated in the procedure specification, at any instance in time one protocol endpoint shall have a
maximum of one ongoing D2CP procedure related to a certain UE.

5.2 D2CP Functions
D2CP functions are defined in D2 GAP TS [2].
5.3 D2CP procedures
5.3.1 Interface Management procedures
5.3.1.1 D2 Setup
The purpose of the D2 Setup procedure is to establish connection with peer O-DUs and exchange the cell level information to
interoperate on the D2 interface. This procedure is the first D2 procedure triggered for the D2-C interface after a TNL
association has become operational.
The procedure uses non-UE associated signalling. This procedure erases any existing D2 related application data associated
with the pair of O-DUs in both the nodes and replaces it by the one received. This procedure also re-initialises the D2 UE-
related contexts (if any) and erases all related signalling connections in the two nodes.

Figure 5.3.1.1-1: D2 Setup, successful operation
As shown in Figure 5.3.1.1-1, the O-DU1 initiates the procedure by sending a D2 SETUP REQUEST message including the
cell information to the O-DU2. The O-DU2 responds with a D2 SETUP RESPONSE message including the cell information.

The received Served Cell List IE in D2 SETUP REQUEST and D2 SETUP RESPONSE messages contains the list of

The O-DU1 and O-DU2 may share Start CRNTI and End CRNTI for the UEs in D2 SETUP REQUEST and D2 SETUP

The O-DUs exchange the D2U Info List IE containing the information for D2-U communication. IP Address and UDP port

D2U PV List IE, received in D2 SETUP REQUEST message indicates the D2 protocol version supported by O-DU1. If O-

The O-DUs stores the T_clearTB timer value exchanged in the D2 SETUP REQUET and D2 SETUP RESPONSE messages.
This timer is used during D2-U procedures. Receiver node shall use T_ClearTB IE when it is operating as sO-DU for the UEs.

Figure 5.3.1.1-2: D2 Setup, unsuccessful operation
If the O-DU2 cannot accept the setup, it shall respond with a D2 SETUP FAILURE message with Cause IE filled with
appropriate cause as shown in Figure 5.3.1.1-2: D2 Setup, unsuccessful operation.
If the O-DU2 does not support any of the protocol version indicated in the D2U PV List IE, procedure will be considered as

If the D2 SETUP FAILURE message includes the Time to wait IE, the O-DU1 shall wait at least for the indicated time before
reinitiating the D2 setup towards the O-DU2.
If the O-DU1 does not receive either D2 SETUP RESPONSE message or D2 SETUP FAILURE message, the O-DU1 may
reinitiate the D2 Setup procedure towards the same O-DU node, provided that the content of the new D2 SETUP REQUEST
message is identical to the content of the previously unacknowledged D2 SETUP REQUEST message.
If the O-DU1 receives a D2 SETUP REQUEST message from the peer entity on the same D2 interface:
-
In case the O-DU1 answers with a D2 SETUP RESPONSE message and receives a subsequent D2 SETUP
FAILURE, the O-DU1 node shall consider the D2 interface as non operational and the procedure as unsuccessfully
terminated.
-
In case the O-DU1 answers with a D2 SETUP FAILURE message and receives a subsequent D2 SETUP RESPONSE
message, the O-DU1 shall ignore the D2 SETUP RESPONSE message and consider the D2 interface as non
operational.

5.3.1.2 D2 Configuration Update
The purpose of the D2 Configuration update procedure is to update the cell configuration in peer O-DU. This procedure may
be triggered by any O-DU in case of modification in configuration of existing cells, release of any existing cell or addition of
new cell. The procedure uses non-UE associated signalling.
In Figure 5.3.1.2-1, O-DU1 is shown as the triggering node for successful completion of configuration update procedure.

Figure 5.3.1.2-1: D2 Setup, successful operation

The O-DU1 initiates the procedure by sending a D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE message to the O-DU2 with the
configuration that needs to be updated. The O-DU2 responds with a D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE
message to confirm that it has successfully updated the configuration data.
The updated configuration data shall be stored in both nodes and used as long as there is an operational TNL association or
until any further update is performed.
If the Served Cell To Add Item IE is contained in the D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE message, the O-DU2 shall store the
information for newly added cell.
If the Served Cells To Modify Item IE is contained in the D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE message, the O-DU2 shall modify
information of existing cell indicated by Old NR CGI IE according to the updated information received in the message.
If the Served Cells To Delete Item IE is contained in the D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE message, the O-DU2 shall delete
the cell information indicated by Old NR CGI IE.
The responding node, O-DU2 shall include, within the Updated Cells Item IE of the D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE
ACKNOWLEDGE message, all cells that were listed in the Served Cell To Add Item and Served Cells To Modify Item IEs of
the D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE message.  For each cell, the Result IE within the Updated Cells Item IE shall indicate
the outcome of the configuration update procedure, explicitly denoting success or failure.
Cells specified in the Served Cells To Delete Item IE of the D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE message shall not be included in
the D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE message.

Figure 5.3.1.2-2: D2 Configuration Update, unsuccessful operation
If the O-DU2 cannot accept the update, or if reconfiguration fails for all the cells, it shall respond with a D2
CONIFGURATION UPDATE FAILURE message with Cause IE filled with appropriate cause as shown in Figure 5.3.1.2-2.

5.3.1.3 D2 Release
The purpose of the D2 Release procedure is to trigger the release of the D2 connection between a pair of O-DUs and erase all
D2 application-level data.
The procedure uses non-UE-associated signaling.
In Figure 5.3.1.3-1, O-DU1 is shown as the triggering node.

Figure 5.3.1.3-1: D2 Release
O-DU1 initiates the procedure by sending the D2 RELEASE REQUEST message to O-DU2. O-DU1 shall include the cause IE
that triggered the release of D2 connection. Upon reception of the D2 RELEASE REQUEST message the O-DU2 shall remove
all resources associated with that D2 connection and all D2 application-level data. The O-DU2 shall reply with the D2
RELEASE RESPONSE message. After receiving the D2 RELEASE RESPONSE message, the O-DU1 shall initiate removal
of the TNL association towards O-DU2 and shall remove all resources associated with that D2 connection and all D2
application-level data.

5.3.2 UE Management procedures
5.3.2.1 UE Addition
The purpose of the UE Addition procedure, as shown in Figure 5.3.2.1-1, is to establish the D2 UE context in the sO-DU by
adding one or more of its cells as SCells for the UEs mentioned in the UE ADDITION REQUEST message. The procedure
uses UE-associated signalling. The pO-DU initiates the procedure by sending UE ADDITION REQUEST message to sO-DU
if it is able to allocate PUCCH resources to receive the CSI information for new SCell. sO-DU responds back with UE
ADDTION RESPONSE message with the information on success or failure of SCell(s) addition for the UE(s) mentioned in the
message.

Figure 5.3.2.1-1: UE Addition Procedure
If sO-DU accepts the request for at least one of candidate SCell(s) listed in SCell To Be Added List IE for the UE(s) present in
UE To Be Added Item IE, it establishes the D2 UE context for the UE(s) and stores the D2 UE ID and C-RNTI. Association
between a UE and D2 UE ID does not change unless D2 UE context is deleted.
If the DRX-Config IE is contained in the UE ADDITION REQUEST message, the sO-DU shall use the provided value from
the pO-DU.
If the MeasGapConfig IE is contained in the UE ADDITION REQUEST message, the sO-DU shall use the provided value
from the pO-DU.

5.3.2.2 UE Modification Update
The purpose of the UE modification update procedure is to modify the established D2 UE Context(s) in sO-DU. As shown in
figure 5.3.2.2-1, pO-DU may initiate this procedure to add a new SCell(s) if it is able to allocate PUCCH resources to receive

Upon reception of the UE MODIFICATION REQUEST message, the sO-DU shall perform the modifications for each

The sO-DU shall consider UE To Be Modified List IE as a list of candidate UE(s) identified by D2 UE ID IE that are requested

If the SCell To AddMod Item IE is contained in the UE MODIFICATION REQUEST message, the sO-DU shall consider SCell

present, each SCell shall not configure the DL MIMO layers exceeding the value indicated by this IE. The cumulative number
of configured DL MIMO layers across all SCells within the sO-DU shall not surpass the maxMIMO-LayersDL-PerDU IE
value. In case of absence of maxMIMO-LayersDL IE in the P O-DU to S O-DU SCell Information, sO-DU can decide to
configure DL MIMO layers in each of the SCells configured for a UE. The sO-DU shall report the total number of layers
allocated for each SCell for the UE using the maxMIMO-LayersUsedDL IE in the S O-DU to P O-DU SCell Information while
sending UE MODIFICATION RESPONSE message.

5.3.2.3 UE Modification Indication
The purpose of the UE Modification Indication procedure is to notify the pO-DU that sO-DU is unable to handle certain
resources (e.g., SCell(s), Logical Channel(s), or UE context) for a UE(s), and hence these resources shall not be used for any
further D2-u communication until reconfigured again.
As shown in Figure 5.3.2.3-1, the sO-DU initiates the procedure by sending UE MODIFICATION INDICATION message to
pO-DU.
Figure 5.3.2.3-1: UE Modification Indication procedure
If UE To Be Updated List IE is contained in the message, the pO-DU shall consider this list as a candidate UE(s) identified by
D2 UE ID IE, that are notified for modification in the UE MODIFICATION INDICATION message.

If the SCell To Be Released Item IE is contained in the UE MODIFICATION INDICATION message, the pO-DU
shall remove the SCell(s) from the D2 UE Context. pO-DU may initiate SCell Deactivation procedure towards UE.
Later if pO-DU decides to add the same SCell again, it may trigger UE Addition or Modification Procedure for
adding the SCell. Cause IE shall indicate the reason of release.

If the LCs To Be Released List IE is contained in the UE MODIFICATION INDICATION message, the pO-DU shall
remove the LC information for the UE from D2 UE Context. These LCs shall not be considered while scheduling data
on the sO-DU. Cause IE shall indicate the reason of release.

If UE To Be Released List IE is contained in the message, pO-DU shall remove the D2 UE context for the UE(s) identified by
D2 UE ID IE. No further communication for the UE(s) shall take place with sO-DU until the UE is added again by the UE
Addition procedure.

The purpose of the UE Reconfiguration Complete procedure is to notify the sO-DU that the UE has successfully completed an
RRC Reconfiguration procedure where SCells that were configured in sO-DU are updated.
As shown in Figure 5.3.2.4-1, pO-DU shall initiate the UE RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE message to sO-DU.

complete from UE.

5.3.2.5 UE Deletion
The purpose of the UE Deletion procedure is to delete the D2 UE Context. This procedure erases any existing UE related
information in sO-DU.
As shown in Figure 5.3.2.5-1, the pO-DU initiates the procedure by sending UE DELETION REQUEST to sO-DU.

Figure 5.3.2.5-1: UE Deletion procedure
The sO-DU shall consider the UE(s) identified by D2 UE ID IE included in UE To Be Deleted List IE to delete the D2 UE
context. sO-DU sends UE DELETION RESPONSE to pO-DU. Any ongoing D2-u procedure will be deleted for the UE and no
new procedure will take place until UE is added again.

5.4.4 Message and information element abstract syntax (with ASN.1)
5.4.4.1 General
D2CP ASN.1 definition conforms to ITU-T Recommendation X.691 [12], ITU-T Recommendation X.680 [13] and ITUT
Recommendation X.681 [14].
The ASN.1 definition specifies the structure and content of D2-C messages. D2CP messages can contain any IEs specified in
the object set definitions for that message without the order or number of occurrences being restricted by ASN.1. However, for
this version of the standard, a sending entity shall construct aD2-C message according to the PDU definitions module and with
the following additional rules:
- IEs shall be ordered (in an IE container) in the order they appear in object set definitions.
- Object set definitions specify how many times IEs may appear. An IE shall appear exactly once if the presence
field in an object has value "mandatory". An IE may appear at most once if the presence field in an object has
value "optional" or "conditional". If in a tabular format there is multiplicity specified for an IE (i.e., an IE list)
then in the corresponding ASN.1 definition the list definition is separated into two parts. The first part defines an
IE container list where the list elements reside. The second part defines list elements. The IE container list
appears as an IE of its own. For this version of the standard an IE container list may contain only one kind of list
elements.

NOTE: In the above "IE" means an IE in the object set with an explicit ID. If one IE needs to appear more than
once in one object set, then the different occurrences will have different IE IDs.

If a D2CP message that is not constructed as defined above is received, this shall be considered as Abstract Syntax
Error, and the message shall be handled as defined for Abstract Syntax Error.

5.4.4.2 Usage of private message mechanism for non-standard use
The private message mechanism for non-standard use is not defined for D2CP messages.

6 D2 User Plane protocol
6.1 D2UP services
The following services are provided by the D2UP protocol:


Provision of D2 sequence number information for user data request and transfer between SCell O-DU and PCell O-
DU.

Request of new user data or retransmission scheduling on SCell O-DU along with the slot Range where UE can be
scheduled in SCell O-DU.

Request for data transfer along with information on allocated DL channel (PDSCH & PDCCH) resources on the
SCell(s)

Provision of sharing PUCCH resource allocation with SCell O-DU.

Information of clearing the MAC TB stored in SCell O-DU once data is transmitted to UE successfully.

Information of clearing the MAC TB once PCell O-DU decides not to continue with further transmission

sharing of the Uplink Control Information received from UE.
6.2 D2UP Functions
The functions of D2UP are described in TS O-RAN.WG5.TS.D2GAP [2].
6.3 D2UP Procedures
6.3.1 Downlink data transfer
6.3.1.1
DL Scheduling Request
The purpose of the DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message as shown in Figure 6.3.1.1-1, is to request sO-DU to schedule the
UE for transmission of the new data or retransmission of the data that is already transmitted on SCell. This message may also
be used for releasing the earlier used HARQ process, if pO-DU decides to abort the retransmission, or to extend the slot range
for UE scheduling in sO-DU. pO-DU sends asynchronous requests to the sO-DU including the cumulated data size in the
Buffer Length IE, that may be scheduled by the sO-DU.
pO-DU may share information for multiple UEs and multiple SCells in a single DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message.
If the pO-DU triggers DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message for a D2 UE ID before reception of DL DATA REQUIRED
message for the same D2 UE ID, it shall set D2 Sched SN IE to 0. Otherwise D2 Sched SN shall be set to the value of D2 Sched
SN received in the latest DL DATA REQUIRED message for t

message for the same D2 UE ID, it shall set D2 Sched SN IE to 0. Otherwise D2 Sched SN shall be set to the value of D2 Sched
SN received in the latest DL DATA REQUIRED message for the UE from sO-DU.

Figure 6.3.1.1-1: DL scheduling request
sO-DU may use D2 UE data size IE to determine the size of information for each UE, identified by D2 UE ID IE, that is
received in DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message.
If the DT IE indicates “reTx”:

If HARQCount IE is not set to zero, HARQStatus IE for each HARQ PID indicates the cause of HARQ failure. sO-
DU shall initiate the retransmission, subject to the allowed range of slots as specified by the SlotOffset and
SlotRange IE, on all the HARQ processes identified by HARQ PID for all the SCells that are included in the
message and identified by SCellIndex IE as defined in 3GPP TS 38.331 clause 6.3.2 [5]. If clearTB IE is set to
TRUE, sO-DU shall delete the stored MAC TB and reuse the HARQ process for further new data transmission.

If HARQCount IE is received as zero, sO-DU shall consider the received message to increase the range of slots, as
specified in SlotRange IE, for the retransmission.
If the DT IE indicates “newTx”:

If LCCount IE is not set to 0, the sO-DU shall determine the SCells using SCell Bitmap IE, where data transmission


If LCCount IE is received as 0, sO-DU shall interpret the received message to increase the range of slots, as specified
in SlotRange/SlotMask IE, for UE scheduling of new transmissions.
If the DT IE indicates “Both”:

DL SCHEDULING REQUEST message shall contain IEs applicable for both reTx and newTx.

Description: Each bit indicates the SCellIndex of the cell where UE is allowed to be scheduled for inter O-DU CA in sO-DU.

Description: Indicates if SlotRange or SlotMask is encoded for UE scheduling in sO-DU. If SlotType indicates presence of

1: indicates that SlotMask is configured for UE scheduling. SlotMask is 36 bit field as defined in section 6.4.3.14
Value range: 0-1
Field length: 1 bit
6.4.3.12

Description: Indicates the slot offset for UE scheduling with respect to receiver slot. sO-DU shall schedule UE after slot offset
only. If value received is 0, it means, UE shall be considered for scheduling from next slot onwards. This is set as per the
highest sub carrier spacing among all the SCells configured for the UE in sO-DU.
Value range: 0-7
Field length: 3 bits

78

6.4.3.13
SlotRange
Description: Continuous range of slots in SCell starting from SlotOffset where UE can be scheduled by the sO-DU. This is
configurable parameter. This is set as per the highest sub carrier spacing among all the SCells configured for the UE in sO-DU.
Value range: 1-50 ( for new transmission) and 1- 31(for retransmission)
Field length: 5 bits for retransmission and 8 bits for new transmission.
6.4.3.14
SlotMask
Description: Indicates the slots starting from SlotOffset where UE can be scheduled in SCell. Either Slot Range or Slot Mask
will be present which is indicated by Slot Type. Each bit indicates the slot where UE can be scheduled by sO-DU. This is set as
per the highest sub carrier spacing among all the SCells configured for the UE in sO-DU.
EXAMPLE 1: SlotOffset = 0, SlotMask = 0x01indicates UE can be scheduled in SCell only in next slot in which the message
is received.
EXAMPLE 2: SlotOffset = 1, SlotMask = 0x01 indicates that UE can only be scheduled in SCell in slot number 2 if message is
received in slot #0.

4.1
D2 interface general principles
37
The general principles for the specification of the D2 interface are as follows:
38

7

-
the D2 interface is open;
1
-
the D2 interface supports the exchange of signalling information between the endpoints. In addition, the interface
2
supports data transmission to the respective endpoints;
3
-
the D2 is a point-to-point interface between the endpoints on two O-DUs. A point-to-point logical interface should be
4
feasible even in the absence of a physical direct connection between the two O-DUs;
5
-
the D2 interface supports control plane (D2-c) and user plane (D2-u) separation;
6
-
the D2 interface enables exchange of UE associated information and non-UE associated information;
7
-
the D2 interface is designed in a future proof way to fulfil new requirements, and services;
8
-
the D2 interface supports NR carrier aggregation of carriers configured in different O-DU nodes. The schedulers in
9
the O-DUs operate independently of each other;
10

The D2 interface provides connectivity between O-DUs to facilitate inter O-DU carrier aggregation. Its functionality is divided

5.2

5.2.1
Interface management function
7
The D2 setup function allows for the initial setup of a D2 connection between two O-DUs, including exchange of the cell-level
8
data. Configuration of the D2 interface endpoints can be managed by the SMO to O-DU via the O1 interface. D2 configuration
9
can also be provided through node specific O&M systems. The D2 setup can be initiated by any O-DU that successfully
10
completes the cell setup procedure. During this process, both the originating and destined O-DUs share cell capabilities, for
11
example sub-carrier spacing, duplexing methods, and TDD DL-UL configurations etc. If received O-DU is unable to accept
12
the D2 connection, D2 SETUP FAILURE is sent back to the transmitting O-DU.
13
Once the D2 connection is established, any changes for the cells used for inter O-DU CA, such as a cell being locked, cell
14
unlocked, overloaded or changes to cell configuration (including cell addition and removal) are communicated to its peer O-
15
DU using the D2 configuration update function. If cell status is changed to locked or disabled, context for all the UEs
16
configured for inter O-DU CA in that SCell is released.
17
D2 release function is used to remove the D2 connection between the two O-DUs, so that all the related resources between the
18
two O-DUs are cleared.
19
The error indication function is used by the O-DU to indicate to the peer O-DU that an error has occurred. For example, if
20
parsing of

e D2 connection between the two O-DUs, so that all the related resources between the
18
two O-DUs are cleared.
19
The error indication function is used by the O-DU to indicate to the peer O-DU that an error has occurred. For example, if
20
parsing of D2 CONFIGURATION UPDATE ACKNOWLEDGE or D2 SETUP RESPONSE fails, O-DU can inform the peer
21
O-DU about the failure using error indication function.

5.2.2
UE management function
1
The UE management function supports the establishment and modification of D2 context for SCells for a UE. These functions
2
include establishment, modification and release of the SCells in PCell and SCell O-DUs. The procedures include addition,
3
deletion or modification of a SCell for a UE in the O-DUs.
4
The establishment of UE addition is initiated by the PCell O-DU. It is accepted or rejected by the SCell O-DU based on the
5
admission control criteria for example resource availability, loading etc. Upon reception of successful addition response for the
6
UE from the SCell O-DU, the PCell O-DU sends UE Context Setup/Modification response to O-CU-CP. RRC Reconfiguration
7
procedure is triggered towards UE for SCell addition. Once RRC Reconfiguration Complete is received from UE, the PCell O-
8
DU sends the UE Reconfiguration Completion message to the SCell O-DU.
9
The modification of SCell configuration for a UE is initiated by the PCell O-DU. If an SCell for a UE is already configured in
10
the SCell O-DU, PCell O-DU can use modification function to add another SCell. The modification function is also used by
11

5.3.2
Transfer of user data
8
Transfer of user data comprises of two functions, the data transfer function and the UCI transfer function.
9
The data transfer function allows the transfer of user data between O-DUs to support inter O-DU carrier aggregation. For DL
10
CA, PCell O-DU sends the user data to SCell O-DU.
11
The data transfer function consists of procedures that allow the exchange of user data, scheduling related information (range of
12
slots) and associated control information between PCell O-DU and SCell O-DU for supporting inter O-DU CA.
13
The PCell O-DU may initiate a procedure to request the SCell O-DU to schedule a user data transmission or to schedule a
14
HARQ retransmission for a particular UE. With each request the PCell O-DU also indicates the range of slots which can be
15
used by the SCell O-DU to schedule new user data or HARQ retransmission. The PCell O-DU may also provide the CSI
16
information to the SCell O-DU. The PCell O-DU may send one or more scheduling requests.
17
The SCell O-DU may reply with the scheduled user data size and/or scheduled HARQ retransmission, as well as the air
18
interface timing details (i.e. slot number). The SCell O-DU may send one or more replies to the PCell O-DU.
19
Requests from the PCell O-DU and replies from the SCell O-DU are sent asynchronously.
20
The PCell O-DU may send the user data matching the scheduled user data size together with the needed PUCCH information
21
to the SCell O-DU.
22
The UCI transfer function enables the PCell O-DU to share CSI reports and/or HARQ feedback to the SCell O-DU. The PCell
23
O-DU may also send a TB clear-flag to indicate that no more re-transmission is needed for a particular HARQ process. Upon
24
reception of the TB clear-flag the SCell O-DU may delete the TB buffer a

and/or HARQ feedback to the SCell O-DU. The PCell
23
O-DU may also send a TB clear-flag to indicate that no more re-transmission is needed for a particular HARQ process. Upon
24
reception of the TB clear-flag the SCell O-DU may delete the TB buffer and reuse the HARQ process ID for a new user data
25
transmission.
